(p-3060) Sūrat al-Tawba

It is Medinan by consensus. It was said: except for its last two verses, "There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves" (9:128), for these two were revealed in Mecca. But this is open to question, for al-Bukhari narrated from al-Bara' that it was the last surah to be revealed. Some scholars excepted what concerns the Prophet, ﷺ, because it was reported that it was revealed regarding his saying to Abu Talib: "I will certainly seek forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from doing so."

It has one hundred and twenty-nine verses, and this surah has ten names:

1- Barā'a (Disavowal): it is so called because it opens with it, and most of what is mentioned in it refers back to it.

2- al-Tawba (Repentance): because of its repetition of the word in it, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So if you repent, it is better for you﴾ (9:3); ﴿But if they repent and establish prayer﴾ (9:11); His saying: ﴿Then Allah relents after that to whom He wills﴾ (9:27); His saying: ﴿And if they repent, it will be better for them﴾ (9:74); His saying: ﴿Perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness﴾ (9:102); His saying: ﴿Allah has certainly relented toward the Prophet﴾ (9:117); His saying the Exalted: ﴿Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance﴾ (9:104); and His saying: ﴿The repentant, the worshippers﴾ (9:112). These two are the most famous of its names.

3- al-Fāḍiḥa (The Disgracer): al-Bukhari narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Surat al-Tawba?" He said: "al-Tawba is al-Fāḍiḥa; it kept on descending: 'And among them... and among them...' until they thought that it would not leave any one of them except that it mentioned him."

4- Surat al-'Adhāb (The Punishment): narrated by al-Hakim from Hudhayfa, because of its repetition of it in it.

5- al-Muqashqasha (The Clearing): narrated by Abu al-Shaykh from Ibn 'Umar. Al-qashqasha means exoneration, and it exonerates from hypocrisy.

6- al-Munaqqira (The Probing): Abu al-Shaykh narrated it from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, because it probed what was in the hearts of the polytheists, i.e., it searched.

7- al-Baḥūth (The Searching): with a fatḥa on the bā', an intensive form; narrated by al-Hakim from al-Miqdad.

8- al-Ḥāfira (The Digging): mentioned by Ibn al-Ghars, because it dug into the hearts of the hypocrites, i.e., searched them, figuratively.

9- al-Muthīra (The Stirring Up): narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim from Qatada, because it stirred up their faults and defects, i.e., brought them out from concealment into the open.

10- al-Mubaʻthira (The Scattering): because it scattered their secrets, i.e., made them manifest.

11- al-Mudamdima (The Destroying): i.e., destroying them.

12- al-Mukhziya (The Humiliating).

13- al-Munakkila (The Punishing): i.e., punishing them.

14- al-Mushharrida (The Dispersing): i.e., driving them away and scattering their gathering.

There is no surah with more names than this one, apart from al-Fātiḥa.

Note:

The early scholars gave several reasons for omitting the basmala at the beginning of this surah and for not pronouncing it:

1-

al-Hakim narrated in al-Mustadrak from Ibn 'Abbas who said: I asked 'Ali ibn Abi Talib: "Why was the basmala not written at the beginning of Bara'a?" He said: "Because it is a guarantee of safety, and Bara'a was revealed with the sword."

That is, its revelation was to lift the guarantee of safety, a status that refuses to begin with what suggests its continuance, namely mention of the Name of Allah the Exalted, accompanied by the attribute of mercy. Hence Ibn 'Uyayna said: "The Name of Allah is peace and safety, so it is not written in the context of repudiation and warfare." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Do not say to one who gives you greeting of peace, "You are not a believer"﴾ (4:94). It was said to him: "But the Prophet ﷺ wrote the basmala to the people of war." He said: "That was only an opening from him, calling them, and he did not repudiate them. Do you not see that he said: 'Peace be upon those who follow guidance'?"

So whoever was called to Allah the Mighty and Majestic and responded, and was called to the jizya and responded, had followed guidance, and the distinction became clear. Likewise al-Mubarrad said: the basmala is an opening for good, and the beginning of this surah is a threat and the breaking of covenants, therefore it was not opened with the basmala.

2- From Ibn 'Abbas who said: "I said to 'Uthman: 'What led you to place al-Anfal, which is among the mathani, and Bara'a, which is among the mi'in, together, and not write the basmala between them, and place them among the seven long ones? What led you to that?' 'Uthman said: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would often be in a time when surahs with many verses were revealed to him, and when something was revealed to him he would call some of those who wrote and say: "Place these verses in the surah in which such-and-such is mentioned." And when a verse was revealed he would say: "Place this verse in the surah in which such-and-such is mentioned." al-Anfal was among the first things revealed at Medina, and Bara'a was among the last of the Qur'an to be revealed, and its story was similar to its story, so I thought it was part of it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died without making clear to us that it was part of it or of something else. For this reason I joined them and did not write the basmala, and placed it among the seven long ones.'" Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it, and al-Tirmidhi said: it is a hasan hadith. Ahmad, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih narrated it, and al-Hakim graded it sahih.

al-Zajjaj said: the resemblance between them is that al-Anfal mentions covenants, and Bara'a mentions their annulment.

3- Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Abu Rawq who said: "al-Anfal and Bara'a are one surah."

Similar was reported from Mujahid, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Sufyan. Ibn Lahi'a said: "They say that Bara'a is from al-Anfal, and for this reason the basmala was not written at the beginning of Bara'a, and [this] resembles the likeness of the two ends and the absence of the basmala." This is refuted by the Prophet ﷺ naming each of them.

al-Hakim said: it is widely transmitted that they are two surahs.

Abu al-Su'ud said: their being well known by these names—i.e., the fourteen names mentioned above—indicates that it is an independent surah and not part of al-Anfal, and the claim that fame is restricted to those who hold it independent is contrary to the apparent sense, end quote.

The author of al-Iqna' reported that the basmala is established for Bara'a in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud, and said: but it is not taken as a basis.

From Malik: when its beginning fell away, the basmala fell away with it. It is established that it was equal to al-Baqara in length, as stated in al-Itqan.

Then know that the readers unanimously agreed to omit the basmala at the end of this surah, following its absence in the orthography of the Imam's codex, except Ibn Minadir, who pronounces it at its beginning, as in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud.

al-Sakhawi said in Jamal al-Qurra': it is well known that its omission at the beginning of Bara'a is practiced.

It is reported from 'Asim that he pronounced the basmala at its beginning, and this is the analogical view. For its omission is either because it was revealed with the sword, or because they did not determine that it was an independent surah but part of al-Anfal. The first reason does not hold, because it is specific to those to whom it was revealed, whereas we pronounce it for blessing. As for starting from what comes after the beginning of Bara'a, there is no text from the earlier leading readers concerning it, and the apparent general statement of many is that one has the choice. al-Sakhawi preferred permissibility, saying: "Do you not see that it is permissible without dispute to say: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, and fight the polytheists'?" Al-Ja'bari held the prohibition, and al-Sakhawi criticized him, saying: "If it is by transmission, it is accepted; otherwise it is rejected, for it is an inference without foundation."

Ibn al-Jazari said in al-Nashr: whoever considers the continuation of the effect of the reason for which the basmala was omitted at its beginning, namely its revelation with the sword, does not pronounce it. Whoever does not consider that, or does not see it, pronounces it without hesitation. And Allah knows best.

And His saying the Exalted:

Discussion of the interpretation of His saying the Exalted:

[1] ﴿A declaration of disavowal from Allah and His Messenger to those with whom you made covenant among the polytheists﴾.

His saying the Exalted: ﴿A declaration of disavowal from Allah and His Messenger to those with whom you made covenant among the polytheists﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, and its tanwin is for magnification, i.e., this is a disavowal; or it is a subject specified by a qualifier, and its predicate is "to those with whom."

Linguistically, al-bara'a is the severing of protection, as one says: "I disavowed so-and-so with a disavowal," meaning the bond of protection between us was severed and no connection remained between us.

If it is said: the right of disavowal is that it be attributed to the covenant-holder, so why was it not attributed to them, but attributed to Allah and His Messenger?

I answer: "you made covenant" is a report of a past event that issued from the Messenger ﷺ and the community, so it was attributed to all, as is the actual case, though it was also by the permission of Allah. As for disavowal, it is a report of a renewed matter, so how could it be attributed to them when they had not yet produced it? It is attributed only to the one who produced it.

al-Nasir said: the secret of this is that attributing the covenant to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ in a context where repudiation is attributed to the polytheists is not fitting in courtesy. Do you not see the instruction of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to the commanders of the expeditions, where he says to them:

"If you alight at a fortress and they ask to come down under the judgment of Allah, do not bring them down under your judgment, for you do not know whether you have hit upon Allah's judgment regarding them or not. But if they ask for the protection of Allah, bring them down under your protection, for that you break your own protection is better than that you break the protection of Allah."

Look at his command ﷺ to honour the protection of Allah, out of fear that it be broken, even though the anticipated matter did not occur afterward. So honouring the covenant of Allah, when the polytheists' breach had been established and Allah and His Messenger had disavowed it, is all the more fitting and deserving that the rejected covenant not be attributed to Allah. For this reason the covenant was attributed to the Muslims rather than the disavowal being attributed to Him.

al-Shihab said: you may say: he attributed the covenant to the Muslims because Allah knew that they had no covenant, so He did not attribute the covenant to Himself, for His disavowal from them and from their covenant is eternal.

This is the subtle point of using the nominal declarative sentence, although it has been said that it is performative, for disavowal from them, and therefore it indicates renewal. End quote.

Ibn Ishaq said: Bara'a was revealed to annul what was between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the polytheists of the covenant they had with him, that no one who came to the House should be hindered, and no one should fear in the sacred month. That was a general covenant between him and the people of polytheism.

Between that there were covenants between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and tribes of the Arabs, specific, for fixed terms. It was revealed concerning this, and concerning those of the hypocrites who stayed behind from him at Tabuk, and concerning the words of those who spoke among them, and Allah uncovered the inner thoughts of peoples who were making light of what they displayed.

Ibn Kathir said: The beginning of this surah was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he returned from the expedition of Tabuk, while they were on the Hajj. Then he mentioned that the polytheists would attend that season in that year as was their custom, and that they circumambulated the House naked. So he disliked mixing with them, and sent Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, as commander of the Hajj that year, to establish the rites for the people, and to inform the polytheists that they should not perform Hajj after that year, and to proclaim to the people: "A declaration of disavowal from Allah and His Messenger." When he departed, he sent after him 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, because he was the one who conveyed on his behalf ﷺ, and because he was of his kin, as will come.

And His saying the Exalted:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 9, verse 2:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[2] ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months, and know that you cannot cause Allah to fail, and that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers.﴾

﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾ That is: say to them, "Travel in the land after our repudiation of the covenant, secure from being killed or fought for a period of four months, and that is from the day of the greater pilgrimage (yawm al-nahr) until ten nights have passed of Rabi' al-Akhir."

The purpose is to grant them security from being killed, and to give them time to reflect and take precautions, so that they will know that after this there is nothing for them but the sword, and so that they will know the strength of the Muslims, since they did not fear their readiness against them.

These four months were a covenant for those who had a covenant of less than four months, so it was completed for them.

As for one who had a covenant for a fixed term, his deadline extends to its term, whatever it may be, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Fulfil their covenant to them until their term﴾ [al-Tawbah: 4], as will come.

This was narrated from more than one source, and Ibn Jarir (Ibn Jarir al-Tabari) chose it. Mujahid said: "This is a deadline for the polytheists in general. Whoever's covenant period was less than four months, it was raised up to that; whoever's was more, it was lowered to that; and whoever had a covenant without a term, he was bound by it. After that he is at war with Allah and His Messenger, to be killed wherever he is found and to be taken captive, unless he repents and believes."

I say: The general wording of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿until their term﴾ [al-Tawbah: 4], is not an objection to this, because one may answer that the idafah (genitive construction) refers to a known covenant, i.e., the known term, which is the four months. And Allah knows best.

﴿And know that you cannot cause Allah to fail﴾ He means that this respite is not due to incapacity on His part regarding you, but for wisdom and kindness toward you; that is, do not think you can escape Him even if He grants you respite. ﴿And that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers﴾ That is, He will humiliate them by killing in this world and by punishment in the Hereafter.

The discussion of the Exalted's saying:

[3] ﴿And a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage that Allah is free of obligation to the polytheists, and so is His Messenger. So if you repent, it is better for you; but if you turn away, then know that you will not cause Allah to escape, and give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment.﴾

﴿And a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage that Allah is free of obligation to the polytheists, and so is His Messenger﴾: (al-adhan) means al-iidhan (the notification), that is, the informing, just as al-aman (safe conduct) and al-ata' (the giving) mean al-iman (granting security) and al-i'ta' (giving).

Its grammatical status is like that of (bara'ah) (a declaration of disavowal), and this sentence is conjoined to a similar one. The difference between the meaning of the first sentence and the second is that the first is a report of the establishment of disavowal, while the second is a report of the obligation to announce what has been established. The disavowal was linked to those among the polytheists who had covenants, while the proclamation was linked to the people, because the disavowal is specific to those bound by treaties and those among them who broke them, whereas the proclamation is general for all people: those who had a covenant and those who did not, and those among the covenant-holders who broke it and those who did not. Thus it is in al-Kashshaf (Zamakhshari's commentary).

As for the day of the greater pilgrimage: it has been said that it is the Day of 'Arafah, and it has been said that it is the Day of Sacrifice (al-Nahr).

Ibn al-Qayyim said: "This is the correct view, because it is established in the two Sahihs that Abu Bakr and 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, made the announcement on the Day of Sacrifice, not on the Day of 'Arafah."

In the Sunan of Abu Dawud, with the most authentic chain, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The day of the greater pilgrimage is the Day of Sacrifice." Likewise Abu Hurayrah and a group of the Companions said so.

The Day of 'Arafah is a prelude to the Day of Sacrifice that precedes it, for on it occur the standing (wuquf), supplication, repentance, entreaty, and steadfastness; then on the Day of Sacrifice occur the delegation and the visit. For this reason its circumambulation is called the Tawaf of Visitation (tawaf al-ziyarah), because they had been purified of their sins on the Day of 'Arafah, then they were permitted on the Day of Sacrifice to visit Him and to enter upon Him at His House. For this reason the sacrifice of offerings, the shaving of heads, the stoning of the jamarat, and most of the acts of Hajj take place on it, and the deeds of the Day of 'Arafah, such as purification and ritual bathing, precede this day. End.

Note:

The scholars have related many reports here, of which we shall mention the principal collections:

Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from Tabuk when he had finished, and he intended to perform Hajj, then he said: 'The polytheists attend and circumambulate naked, so I do not like to perform Hajj,' so that this would not occur. He sent Abu Bakr and 'Ali, and they went around among the people at Dhu al-Majaz and at their marketplaces where they used to trade, and at all the seasons. They announced to the people of covenants that they should be secure for four months, which are the consecutive months: twenty days of Dhu al-Hijjah, up to ten days of Rabi' al-Akhir. After that there is no covenant for them. And he announced to all the people war, until they accept faith."

Ibn Ishaq related with his chain from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali, may Allah's good pleasure be upon him, who said: "When [Bara'ah] was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he had sent Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, to establish the Hajj for the people. It was said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, if only you would send it to Abu Bakr!' He said: 'None shall deliver on my behalf except a man from my household.' Then he called 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah's good pleasure be upon him, and said to him: 'Go out with this account from the beginning of Bara'ah, and announce to the people on the Day of Sacrifice when they gather at Mina, that no disbeliever will enter Paradise, no polytheist will perform Hajj after this year, no one will circumambulate the House naked, and whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, it is his until its term.'

So 'Ali ibn Abi Talib went out on the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, al-'Adba', until he overtook Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. When Abu Bakr saw him on the road, he said: 'Is it a commander or one commanded?' He said: 'Rather, one commanded.' Then they went on. Abu Bakr led the people in Hajj, and the Arabs in that year were in their positions of Hajj which they had followed in the Jahiliyyah. When the Day of Sacrifice came, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, stood up and announced to the people what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had commanded him, saying: 'O people, no disbeliever will enter Paradise, no polytheist will perform Hajj after this year, no one will circumambulate the House naked, and whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, it is his until its term.'

He gave the people a term of four months from the day he announced to them, so that every people might return to their refuge and lands. Then there is no covenant or protection for a polytheist, except one who had a covenant with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for a fixed term, for him it is until its term. So no polytheist performed Hajj after that year, and no one circumambulated the House naked.

Then they both returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

Ibn Ishaq said: This was the matter of [Bara'ah] concerning those among the polytheists who had a covenant that year, and those with a term until the specified time.

Al-Bukhari related from Abu Hurayrah who said: "Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, sent me in that Hajj among the announcers, sending them on the Day of Sacrifice to announce at Mina: 'No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked.'"

Humayd said: "Then the Prophet ﷺ made 'Ali ibn Abi Talib ride behind him, and commanded him to announce Bara'ah."

Abu Hurayrah said: "'Ali announced with us to the people of Mina on the Day of Sacrifice the Bara'ah, and that no polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked."

In another narration of al-Bukhari, Abu Hurayrah said: "Abu Bakr sent me among those who announce on the Day of Sacrifice at Mina: No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked. The Day of the Greater Pilgrimage is the Day of Sacrifice. It was called 'the Greater' because of the people's saying, regarding -the 'Umrah- the lesser Hajj. So Abu Bakr renounced to the people in that year, and no polytheist performed Hajj in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed Hajj." This is the wording of al-Bukhari in the "Book of Jihad."

Imam Ahmad related "from Abu Hurayrah who said: I was with 'Ali ibn Abi Talib when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him to the people of Makkah with Bara'ah. He said: 'What were you proclaiming?' He said: 'We were proclaiming: No one who disbelieves will enter Paradise, no one will circumambulate the House naked, and whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, its term is four months. When the four months pass, Allah is free of obligation to the polytheists, and so is His Messenger, and no polytheist shall perform Hajj to this House after this year.'" He said: "I kept proclaiming until my voice became hoarse." (Sahila al-rajul and sahila sawtuh: became hoarse.)

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So if you repent, it is better for you﴾: i.e., if you repent, O polytheists, from your disbelief and return to the Oneness of Allah and sincerity in worship to Him alone, without the gods and rivals, then it is better for you than persisting in polytheism, the head of error and corruption. ﴿But if you turn away﴾: i.e., from faith, and you refuse except to persist in your error and polytheism. ﴿Then know that you will not cause Allah to escape﴾: i.e., you will not escape His seizing and His punishment. ﴿And give tidings to those who disbelieve﴾: i.e., who denied your prophethood and opposed the command of their Lord ﴿of a painful punishment﴾: i.e., a torment that is grievous and will befall them.

In this there is mockery and threat to the extent that it contains, lest one think that if the punishment of this world passed away and ceased, they would be saved from punishment; rather, punishment is prepared for them on the Day of Resurrection.

Then the Exalted excepted those who had a covenant without limit, from the period of four months' respite, and those who had a covenant limited to its appointed term, which they had been bound to, so He, glorified is He, said:

The discussion of the statement of Allah the Exalted:

[4] ﴿Except those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists, then they have not failed you in anything, nor have they supported anyone against you. So fulfill for them their covenant until their term.~ Indeed, Allah loves the righteous.﴾

﴿Except those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists, then they have not failed you in anything﴾ That is: in any of the conditions of the pact, so they did not kill any of you, nor did they harm you in any way.

Abu al-Su'ud said: It is also read with the dotted letter (qaf-dotted, i.e., "yanqusu" with the nun-qaf-dhad sequence changed to the dotted form), meaning: they did not break your covenant in anything, from (al-naqd, "breaking"). The word (thumma, "then"), serves to indicate their steadfastness in their covenant despite the lapse of time. ﴿Nor have they supported﴾ That is: they did not aid ﴿anyone against you﴾ That is: any enemy from among your enemies.

﴿So fulfill for them their covenant until their term.﴾ Then the Exalted urged fulfillment of this, alerting that it is of the category of piety, with His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the righteous.﴾ That is: so be mindful of Him in this matter.

[p. 3072]

**The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words:**

[5] ﴿And when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them, and seize them, besiege them, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush. But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then let them go their way. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿When ... has passed﴾ means: has ended. ﴿The sacred months﴾ means: those in which the covenant-holders were permitted to travel freely through the land, and in which fighting against them was forbidden. ﴿Kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ means: whether in the sacred precinct (ḥill) or in the sacred territory (ḥaram), as said by more than one scholar.

Ibn Kathir said: This is a general command, but the commonly held view is that it is restricted to other than the sacred territory (ḥaram), because fighting is forbidden there, based on His saying: ﴿And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque until they fight you there. But if they fight you, then kill them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 191].

﴿And seize them﴾ means: take them captive. ﴿And besiege them﴾ means: confine them to the place where they are, so that they do not spread throughout the lands. ﴿And lie in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾ means: for fighting them, at every road and passage. ﴿But if they repent﴾ means: from disbelief, ﴿and establish prayer and give zakah, then let them go their way﴾ means: then cease to harass them. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ means: He forgives them what has passed of disbelief and treachery.

**Notes:**

**First:** What we have mentioned, that the intended meaning of "the sacred months" (al-ashhur al-ḥuram) is the months of the covenant, is the view chosen by most scholars.

They were called ḥuram (sacred) because fighting against the polytheists and shedding their blood is forbidden in them. The alif and lam (الألف واللام) here indicate a specific reference (lil-ʿahd), and the placing of the explicit noun in place of a pronoun is to make it a means of describing them as sacred, emphasising what is implied by the permission to travel freely: the prohibition of harming them, together with the greater attention given to their matter.

It has been said: the intended "sacred months" are Rajab, Dhu al-Qiʿdah, Dhu al-Ḥijjah, and al-Muḥarram. This was narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Ḍaḥḥak and al-Bāqir, and Ibn Jarir (al-Ṭabari) chose it.

This view is held to be weak, because the noble wording does not support it, since the particle fa (then) which links the command to the months contradicts it. It conflicts with the context, which requires that these months be consecutive.

Ibn al-Qayyim said: The ḥuram here are the months of the tasyīr (the free-travel period). The first of them is the day of the proclamation (al-adhān), which is the tenth of Dhu al-Ḥijjah, the Day of the Greater Pilgrimage, on which the proclamation of this was made, and the last of them is the tenth of Rabiʿ al-Akhir. These are not the four months mentioned in His saying: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah, the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them four are sacred. That is the correct religion﴾ [al-Tawbah: 36]. Those are one single month (Rajab) and three consecutive months (Dhu al-Qiʿdah and the two that follow it).

He did not grant the polytheists free travel during these four months, because that is impossible, since they are not consecutive. He had only given them a deadline of four months, and then after their expiry He commanded him to fight them. End of quotation.

They (the scholars) said: It follows from this view that the sanctity of those months remains, and that the answer requires saying it has been abrogated (naskh), either by a consensus (ijmaʿ) on that, or by what is authentically reported, that the Prophet (ﷺ) besieged Ṭāʾif ten nights before the end of al-Muḥarram. However, this consensus is itself a matter of discussion, since some scholars disagreed about the continuation of its sanctity, but they did not consider that disagreement significant, as stated in al-ʿInāyah.

In it (al-ʿInāyah) also: You may say that the prohibition of fighting in the sacred months of that year does not require its prohibition in every similar period. Rather, that is left unaddressed, so it does not contradict the consensus, and its permissibility is known from another evidence.

I say: This second view appears correct to me, and that the intended four months are the well-known ones, and that His saying ﴿when the sacred months have passed﴾ refers to these four, because wherever they are mentioned in the revelation they refer only to these, so diverting them to other months requires a conclusive proof.

In Fath al-Bayan it is said: The meaning of the verse on this view is the obligation to refrain from fighting those polytheists who have no covenant during these sacred months. The proclamation and the renunciation of covenants to the polytheists took place on the Day of Sacrifice (yawm al-nahr), so the remaining sacred months, which are the three consecutive ones, were fifty days, and they end with the end of the month of al-Muḥarram. Then Allah commanded them to kill the polytheists wherever they are found, and a group of the people of knowledge held this. End of quotation.

It cannot be said that the remaining sacred months were eighty days, because the Hajj in that year fell on the tenth of Dhu al-Qiʿdah due to the nasiʾ (the intercalation practice of the pagan Arabs). Then in the following year it fell on the tenth of Dhu al-Ḥijjah, and in that year the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed the Hajj and said: "Indeed, time has revolved (istadāra)..." the hadith. This is because we say: in that year Dhu al-Qiʿdah was, by their reckoning, Dhu al-Ḥijjah, not in reality; and likewise Dhu al-Ḥijjah and al-Muḥarram. So they were treated according to their reckoning.

**Second:** Al-Suyuti said in al-Iklil, regarding His saying ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾: This is the verse of the sword (āyat al-sayf), which abrogates the verses of pardon, forgiveness, turning away and peace. End of quotation.

It is reported from al-Ḍaḥḥak that it was abrogated by His saying in Surah Muhammad: ﴿Then either release them as a favour or ransom them﴾ [Muhammad: 4].

Al-Ḥākim refuted this, saying: There is no doubt that Bara'ah (al-Tawbah) was revealed after Surah Muhammad. The implication of al-Ḥākim's statement is that it is neither an abrogating nor an abrogated verse. He said: Because combining them without contradiction is possible. So wherever mention of turning away occurs in the Qur'an, what is meant is the turning away of rejection, not of approval. As for capture and ransom, what is meant is that the Imam has a choice between them, not that killing is mandatory. For if killing were mandatory, taking captives would have no meaning after killing. End of quotation.

Its general scope includes the polytheists of the Arabs and others. And He His saying ﴿And seize them, besiege them, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾ is taken as evidence for the permissibility of besieging them, raiding them, and attacking them by night.

**Third:** From His saying ﴿But if they repent...﴾ and the verse, it follows that the command to let them go their way is conditional upon three requirements: repentance, establishing prayer, and paying zakah. So where these are not fulfilled, what has been mentioned before, namely killing, seizing and besieging, is permitted.

For this reason, al-Ṣiddīq (Abu Bakr), may Allah be pleased with him, relied on this noble verse and similar ones in fighting those who withheld zakah.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: May Allah have mercy on Abu Bakr; how learned in jurisprudence he was!

In the two Ṣaḥīḥs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "I have been commanded to fight people until they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and establish prayer and pay zakah."

Imam Aḥmad narrated from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been commanded to fight people until they testify that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. When they have testified, faced our qiblah, eaten our slaughtered animals, and prayed our prayer, then their blood and their property are made sacred to us, except by their right. They have what the Muslims have, and they have the obligations the Muslims have." Narrated by al-Bukhari and others.

**Fourth:** Ibn al-Qayyim mentioned a wonderful summary, in the context of the order of the Prophet's (ﷺ) conduct towards the disbelievers and hypocrites, from the time he was sent until he met Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, which supports the understanding of what this surah indicates. He, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

The first thing revealed to him by his Lord, blessed and exalted, was that he should read in the name of his Lord who created. That was the beginning of his prophethood. He was commanded to read to himself, and at that time he was not commanded to convey. Then He revealed to him: ﴿O you wrapped in garments﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 1] ﴿Arise and warn﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 2]. He made him a prophet by His saying ﴿Read﴾ [al-ʿAlaq: 1], and sent him with ﴿O you wrapped in garments﴾. Then He commanded him to warn his closest kinsfolk, then to warn his people, then to warn those around them of the Arabs, then to warn all the Arabs, then to warn all mankind. So he remained for about ten years after his prophethood, warning by the call, without fighting and without jizyah (poll tax), and he was commanded to restrain, to be patient, and to pardon. Then he was permitted to emigrate, and was permitted to fight. Then he was commanded to fight whoever fought him, and to refrain from those who did not fight him. Then he was commanded to fight the polytheists until the religion is entirely for Allah. Then after the command to strive (jihad), the disbelievers with him were of three categories: people of truce and armistice, people of war, and people of protected status (dhimmah).

So he was commanded to fulfil the covenant of the people of the agreement and truce, and to keep it for them as long as they stood by the covenant. If he feared treachery from them, he would renounce the covenant with them, and he would not fight them until he informed them of the breaking of the covenant. He was commanded to fight whoever broke his covenant. When Surah Bara'ah (al-Tawbah) was revealed, it came explaining the rulings of all these categories. In it He commanded him to fight the enemies among the People of the Book until they pay jizyah or enter Islam.

In it He also commanded him to strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and to be harsh towards them. He strove against the disbelievers with the sword and the spear, and against the hypocrites with argument and speech. In it He commanded him to disassociate from the covenants of the disbelievers and to renounce their covenants towards them. He divided the people of covenant in this regard into three categories: a category he commanded him to fight, namely those who broke his covenant and did not remain upright towards him, so he fought them and overcame them.

A category who had a fixed-term covenant which they had not broken and had not supported anyone against him; he commanded him to fulfil their covenant until its term.

And a category who had no covenant and had not fought him, or who had an open-ended covenant; he commanded him to give them a deadline of four months, and after its expiry commanded him to fight them.

So he killed the one who broke his covenant, gave a four-month respite to those who had no covenant or an open-ended covenant, and commanded him to fulfil the covenant of the one who kept his covenant until its term. All of these embraced Islam, and did not remain upon their disbelief until their term. He imposed jizyah on the people of protected status. Thus, after the revelation of Bara'ah, the matter of the disbelievers with him became settled in three categories: those at war with him, people of covenant, and people of protected status.

Then the condition of the people of covenant and truce ended in Islam, so they became with him two categories: those at war, and people of protected status. Those at war with him were in fear of him. So the people of the earth became with him three categories: a Muslim believer in him, one at peace with him and secure, and one in fear and at war.

As for his conduct towards the hypocrites: he was commanded to accept their outward profession, and to leave their inner states to Allah, and to strive against them with knowledge and argument. He was commanded to turn away from them, to be harsh with them, and to address their souls with an eloquent word. He was forbidden to pray over them or to stand at their graves. He was informed that whether he asked forgiveness for them or did not ask forgiveness for them, Allah would not forgive them. This was his conduct towards his enemies among the disbelievers and the hypocrites. End of quotation.

**And His, may He be exalted, words:**

The discussion of the words of God, the Exalted:

[6] ﴿And if any one of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection so that he may hear the words of God; then convey him to his place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know.﴾

That is: if one of the polytheists whom you were commanded to fight seeks your protection, that is, asks you for safe conduct after the expiry of the months of the covenant, then grant him what he asks, until he hears the words of God, that is, the Qur'an which you recite to him, and reflects upon it, and comes to know the reality of the matter, and the proof of God is established against him through it. If he becomes Muslim, he is granted what belongs to the Muslims; and if he refuses, he is returned to his place of safety and his home, where he is secure, and then fight him if you wish.

As for His words, the Exalted: ﴿That﴾, meaning the command to grant protection and to convey him to his place of safety, ﴿is because they are a people who do not know﴾, that is, ignorant, so it is necessary to give them security until they hear and understand the truth, and no excuse remains for them.

Remarks:

First: The verse indicates that the one who seeks safe conduct is not to be harmed, and that he is to be enabled to return without treachery or betrayal toward him. For this reason, there came in the warning against failing to keep a covenant and against treachery what restrains in the strongest terms.

Al-Bukhari in (his "Tarikh") and al-Nasa'i narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever grants security to a man for his blood and then kills him, I am innocent of the killer, even if the one killed was a disbeliever."

Ahmad and the two Shaykhs narrated from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "For every treacherous one there will be a banner by which he is known on the Day of Resurrection."

Ibn Kathir said: Whoever comes from the abode of war to the abode of Islam, for conveying a message, or for trade, or seeking a truce or a armistice, or bringing the jizya, or the like of such reasons, and asks the Imam or his deputy for safe conduct, is granted it, for as long as he moves about in the abode of Islam, until he returns to his place of safety and homeland.

Al-Hakim said: He is only granted protection and security if it is not known that he seeks deception and cunning, because He, the Exalted, made the obligation of granting protection conditional by His saying: ﴿until he hears the words of God﴾.

Second: Al-Hakim said: The verse indicates that it is permissible for a disbeliever to enter the mosque in order to hear the words of God.

Third: Those who hold that the speech of God is with a letter and a sound that are eternal, namely the Hanbalites and those who agree with them such as al-Adud, have used this verse as evidence.

They said: Because the literal sense of the verse indicates that the words of God are heard by the disbeliever, the believer, the heretic and the truthful, and what the majority of creation hears is nothing but these letters and sounds.

Thus it is shown that the words of God are not these letters and sounds, and the claim that the words of God are something other than them is false, because the Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not intend by his saying "the words of God" anything but them. Al-Razi acknowledged the strength of this, as a means of refuting whoever disagrees with it. What has passed for us regarding His words, "And God spoke to Moses with speech" [al-Nisa: 164], at the end of Surat al-Nisa, refer back to it.

Fourth: Al-Razi said: The verse indicates that imitation (taqlid) is not sufficient in religion, and that reflection and reasoned inference are necessary. This is because if imitation were sufficient, this disbeliever would not have been granted a respite; rather it would be said to him: either you believe, or we will kill you. Since he was not told that, but was instead given a respite, and fear was removed from him, and it became obligatory to convey him to his place of safety, it is known that this is because imitation is not sufficient in religion, and that proof and evidence are necessary. Therefore he was given time so that reflection and inference could take place for him.

Then God, the Exalted, explained His wisdom in the disavowal of the polytheists, and His granting them a respite of four months, after which came the drawn sword, by His saying:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[7] ﴿How can there be a covenant for the polytheists with Allah and with His Messenger, except for those with whom you made a covenant at al-Masjid al-Haram? So as long as they are upright toward you, be upright toward them. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous.﴾

﴿How can there be a covenant for the polytheists﴾ i.e., a guarantee of safety, ﴿with Allah and with His Messenger﴾ i.e., while they are disbelievers in both of them. So the interrogative is in the sense of denial and disapproval of their having a covenant. ﴿except for those with whom you made a covenant at al-Masjid al-Haram﴾ meaning the people of Makkah, whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a covenant with on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah to abstain from war with them for ten years. ﴿So as long as they are upright toward you, be upright toward them﴾ i.e., as long as they remain upright in their covenant, observing your rights, then you be upright toward them in their covenant.

﴿Indeed, Allah loves the righteous﴾ i.e., so fear Him by breaking the covenant of those who remain upright in their covenant.

Ibn Kathir said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims did that. The agreement and truce with the people of Makkah continued from Dhu al-Qa'dah of the sixth year until Quraysh broke the covenant and backed their allies, Banu Bakr, against Khuza'ah, the allies of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they killed them in the Sacred Precinct as well. At that point the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) campaigned against them in Ramadan of the eighth year, and Allah granted him the sacred city, and empowered him over them, and to Allah belongs praise and grace. So he freed those of them who embraced Islam after subjugation and domination over them, and they were called the Tulaqa' (the freed ones), and they numbered about two thousand. As for those who persisted in their disbelief and fled from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he sent them a guarantee of safety and a grace period of four months, to go wherever they wished. Among them were Safwan ibn Umayyah, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl and others. Then Allah guided them to Islam.

And His saying, exalted is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 9, verse 8:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[ 8 ] ﴿How (can there be a covenant with them)? And if they gain the upper hand over you, they will not observe regarding you any tie of kinship or pact. They satisfy you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse, and most of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾

﴿How, and if they gain the upper hand over you﴾ means: if they triumph over you, after what preceded from their affirmation of oaths and covenants, ﴿they will not observe regarding you any tie of kinship (ilan) nor any pact (dhimmah)﴾. That is, ilan means kinship and oath, and dhimmah means covenant.

This sentence is linked to the previous verse, meaning: how can they have a covenant when their condition is what has been mentioned? In it there is an incitement for the believers to disassociate themselves from them, because whoever is watching for an opportunity and waiting for it cannot be expected to keep a covenant continuously.

Al-Nasir said: Since the discussion lengthened with the exception of those who remained faithful to the covenant, "how" (kayfa) was repeated to refresh the mention and so that part of the speech would hold onto part of it. End of quote.

Then Exalted is He resumed explaining their condition, which contradicts their steadfastness to the covenant, with His saying: ﴿They satisfy you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse﴾, meaning: what their mouths utter. ﴿And most of them are defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning: rebellious, having neither a creed that restrains them nor a sense of honor that deters them.

The specification of "most" is because some of the disbelievers avoid excuses and abstain from what leads to a reputation for evil.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[9] ﴿They have sold the signs of Allah for a small price, and so they have averted [people] from His way. Indeed, evil is what they used to do.﴾

﴿They have sold the signs of Allah﴾ means: they exchanged them ﴿for a small price﴾, that is, for some of the goods of this world, meaning their corrupt desires (p-3081). ﴿And so they averted [people] from His way﴾ means: they turned away from it, or they diverted others from it. ﴿Indeed, evil is what they used to do.﴾

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[10] ﴿They do not observe regarding a believer ties of kinship or a covenant, and those are the transgressors.﴾

﴿They do not observe regarding a believer ties of kinship or a covenant, and those are the transgressors.﴾ That is: those who exceed the limit in wrongdoing and evil deeds.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[11] ﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion. And We detail the verses for a people who know.﴾

﴿But if they repent﴾, i.e., from the disbelief they are upon, ﴿and establish prayer and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion﴾, i.e., they are your brothers: they have what you have, and they bear what you bear. So treat them with the treatment due to brothers. In this there is, regarding winning them over and attracting their hearts, something beyond which there is no further degree.

His words ﴿And We detail the verses for a people who know﴾ are a parenthetical sentence (jumlah mu'taridah) urging reflection upon what was detailed of the rulings concerning the treaty-bound polytheists (al-mushrikin al-mu'ahidin), and urging the preservation of them.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[12] ﴿And if they break their oaths after their covenant and attack your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief. Indeed, they have no oaths, so that they may desist.﴾

﴿And if they break﴾, i.e., violate, ﴿their oaths after their covenant and attack your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief﴾, i.e., fight them.

The noble composition chose this wording to indicate that by doing so they had become leaders and foremost figures in disbelief, deserving of being killed and fought.

It has been said: the intended meaning of "the leaders" is their chiefs and their mighty men. Singling them out for mention is either because of the great importance of killing them, or to prevent [the believers] from showing them leniency, or because they are the ones likely to be such, or to indicate their complete eradication, for their killing usually occurs after the killing of those beneath them. This was reported by Abu al-Su'ud.

﴿Indeed, they have no oaths﴾, plural of yamin (oath), i.e., they have no covenants in reality, since they do not honor them and do not regard breaking them as something to be avoided. Thus, even if they utter them, they carry no weight.

It was also read as (lā īmāna), with a kasra on the hamza, meaning: they have no Islam, and no sincere affirmation, until they refrain from breaking [their word] and from attacking. ﴿So that they may desist﴾, i.e., from disbelief and attacking, and return to faith.

Note:

al-Suyuti said in (al-Iklil): Whoever holds that a dhimmi (a non-Muslim living under the protection of the Islamic state) is to be killed if he attacks Islam, the Qur'an, or speaks ill of the Prophet (ﷺ), whether or not the breaking of the covenant was stipulated, has relied on this verse. Whoever holds that their repentance is accepted has relied on His saying: ﴿so that they may desist﴾. End of quote.

Then He urged fighting them by stirring the hearts of the believers and inciting them, with His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion of His words, exalted is He:

[13] ﴿Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths and resolved to expel the Messenger, and they began the attack against you the first time? Do you fear them? Yet Allah has more right that you fear Him, if you are believers.﴾

﴿Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths﴾, meaning the oaths they swore in the treaty. ﴿And resolved to expel the Messenger﴾, meaning from Makkah, when they gathered in the Dar al-Nadwa (the assembly house of the Quraysh), as mentioned in His words, exalted is He: ﴿And [recall] when those who disbelieved plotted against you﴾ [al-Anfal: 30]. This is then a reproach to them for their earlier crime. ﴿And they began the attack against you the first time﴾, meaning by fighting, on the day of Badr, when they went out to defend others. When they did not escape and knew of it, they persisted in their course seeking combat, out of insolence and arrogance.

It was said: [it refers] to their breaking of the covenant and their fighting alongside their allies, the Bani Bakr, against the Khuza'a, who were allies of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) marched against them in the year of the Conquest, and what happened happened. This was said by Ibn Kathir.

Al-Zamakhshari said: That is, they are the ones from whom the initiation of fighting came, because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) first came to them with the clear Book and challenged them with it. They turned away from opposing it, being unable to do so, and resorted to fighting. Thus they are the ones who initiated the fighting, and the initiator is the wrongdoer. So what prevents you from fighting them with the same, and from striking them with evil as they struck you?

﴿Do you fear them?﴾, meaning: do you fear that some harm from them will befall you, so that you abandon fighting them? ﴿Yet Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾ by opposing His command and abandoning the fight against them. ﴿If you are believers﴾, meaning: the requirement of sound faith is that the believer fears none but his Lord and does not care for anyone else, as in His words, exalted is He: ﴿And they fear none but Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 39]. This was said by al-Zamakhshari. In it is a severity that is not hidden.

Then, exalted is He, resolved upon the believers the command to fight, for His wisdom, by His words:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 9, verse 14:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[14] ﴿Fight them, and Allah will punish them by your hands, and disgrace them, and give you victory over them, and heal the breasts of a believing people.﴾

﴿Fight them, and Allah will punish them﴾, i.e., with the pain of wounds and death; ﴿by your hands﴾, i.e., by giving you dominance over them; ﴿and disgrace them﴾, i.e., by capture and enslavement, so that both physical and moral punishment are combined for them; ﴿and give you victory over them and heal the breasts of a believing people﴾, i.e., of those who did not witness the fighting.

(p-3084) On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[15] ﴿And He will remove the rage from their hearts. And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾

﴿And He will remove the rage from their hearts﴾ — meaning: by what they endured of hardships and plots. ﴿And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills﴾ — meaning: so that you obtain their reward. ﴿And Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾ — meaning: in His actions and His commands.

Allah, glorified is He, has fulfilled all these promises for them. Therefore His informing the Prophet (ﷺ) of this before it occurred was a great miracle, indicating his truthfulness and the soundness of his prophethood.

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[16] ﴿Or did you think that you would be left alone while Allah has not yet made evident those among you who strove and did not take, other than Allah and His Messenger and the believers, any intimate (walījah)?  And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾

﴿Or did you think that you would be left alone﴾ — i.e., in the state you are in, and that you would not be commanded to fight (jihād). ﴿while Allah has not yet made evident those among you who strove and did not take, other than Allah and His Messenger and the believers, any intimate (walījah)﴾ — i.e., any confidant (biṭānah) to whom they reveal their secrets.

The waw in (wa-lammā) is circumstantial (ḥāliyyah), and (lammā) is for negation with expectation (lil-nafy ma'a al-tawaqquʿ). What is intended by the negation of knowledge is the negation of the thing known by way of demonstrative proof, for if it had caught the scent of existence, it would have known it with certainty; so when it did not know, its non-existence necessarily follows with certainty. ﴿and did not take﴾ is a conjunction with ﴿strove﴾ and falls within the scope of the relative clause. The meaning is: you will not be left in the state you are in, while the sincere among the fighters from among you have not yet been distinguished from others; rather, you must be tested until the sincere among you become manifest, and they are those who strove in the way of Allah, for the sake of Allah, and did not take an intimate, i.e., a confidant, from among those who oppose the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers, may Allah be pleased with them. (Lammā) indicates that the distinguishing and clarifying of that is expected and certain to occur, and that those who did not make their religion sincerely for Allah will be separated from the sincere. In the verse, one of the two categories is left implicit, as it does not mention the negligent, because they are far removed from being included under the will of the Most Generous of the generous. This is like the saying of the poet:

؎ And I do not know, when I set out for a land, seeking good, which of the two will befall me.

(p-3085) Allah the Exalted has said in another verse: ﴿Alif. Lām. Mīm.﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 1] ﴿Do people think that they will be left alone on saying "We believe" and that they will not be tested?﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 2] ﴿And We certainly tested those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars.﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 3] And Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 142], the verse, and He the Exalted has said: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 179], the verse. All of them indicate that the legislation of jihād is a test that distinguishes the obedient from others.

And the saying of Allah the Exalted:

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[17] ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while they testify against themselves to disbelief. Those — their deeds have become worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally.﴾

﴿It is not for the polytheists﴾, meaning: it is not right or proper for them, ﴿to maintain the mosques of Allah﴾, meaning those built for His name alone, with no partner for Him. That is, they should not maintain any part of them. It is a plural noun in construct (jam' mudaf) within a negative context, and it includes the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram) by primary inclusion, since the negation of a plural indicates negation of every individual, so its negation applies to the specific individual by way of implication (kinayah). It is also read as (masjid Allah) in the singular, explicitly stating the intended meaning, which is the Sacred Mosque, the most noble of the mosques on earth, which was built on the first day for the worship of Allah alone, with no partner, and was founded by the Friend of the Most Merciful (Khalil al-Rahman, i.e., Ibrahim, peace be upon him).

In al-Basair (al-Basair, a work of lexicography), it is said: (ya'muru) may derive either from 'imarah, which is the preservation of a building, or from 'umrah, which is visiting, or from the saying "I 'amartu bi-makan kadha," meaning "I resided in such a place." End of quote.

﴿testify against themselves to disbelief﴾, meaning: by their condition and their statements. This is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun in ﴿ya'muru﴾ (p. 3086).

﴿Those — their deeds have become worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally﴾. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And what is wrong with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar people from the Sacred Mosque, and they were not its guardians? Its guardians are only the God-fearing﴾ [al-Anfal: 34]. For this reason, exalted is He, said:

The Discussion of the Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[18] ﴿Indeed, only those will maintain the mosques of Allah who believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish prayer, give zakat, and fear none but Allah. It is those who are expected to be among the guided.﴾

﴿Indeed, only those will maintain the mosques of Allah who believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish prayer, give zakat, and fear none but Allah﴾, meaning: they worship none but Allah. ﴿It is those who are expected to be among the guided﴾, meaning: to Paradise.

The presentation of their being guided, together with the noble qualities they possess, in the form of expectation, serves to cut off the hopes of the disbelievers of reaching the stations of guidance and of benefiting from their deeds, which they reckon to be good deeds, and to rebuke them by making them certain that they are guided. For if the believers, who possess these perfections, have their matter hanging between "perhaps" (la'alla) and "expectedly" (asa), then what of the disbelievers, who are what they are, with deeds that are what they are?! In it there is also gentleness toward the believers, and encouragement for them to give precedence to the side of fear over the side of hope, and to reject being deceived about Allah, exalted is He. - Thus has Abu al-Su'ud written it -.

And al-Nasir said: Most of them say that "asa" (expectedly) from Allah is obligatory, on the basis that its use is not diverted to the addressees.

The truth is that the address is directed to them, as al-Zamakhshari said; that is, the state of these believers is a state whose outcome is hoped for and known with God, and with Allah is the outcome of affairs.

(p-3087) Admonitions:

The first: al-Zamakhshari said: "Maintenance" (al-'imarah) encompasses repairing what has fallen into disrepair of it and its upkeep, cleaning it and lighting it with lamps, glorifying it and making it habitual for worship and remembrance, and among remembrance is the study of knowledge, indeed it is its most sublime and greatest form, and guarding it from what mosques were not built for, of worldly talk, let alone idle talk.

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever goes to the mosque in the morning or in the evening, Allah prepares for him a lodging in Paradise every time he goes in the morning or in the evening."

Both of them also narrated from Uthman ibn Affan, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever builds a mosque for Allah, seeking thereby the face of Allah, the Exalted, Allah builds for him a house in Paradise."

al-Tirmidhi narrated from Abu Sa'id that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you see a man habitually attending the mosque, then bear witness to his faith," and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, only those will maintain the mosques of Allah﴾, the verse.

The second: The reason the belief in the Messenger (ﷺ) is not mentioned is that it is included in belief in Allah; it was omitted for emphasis in mentioning belief in the message, indicating that they are like one thing: when one of them is mentioned, the other is understood. Moreover, by mentioning the origin and the return, it is indicated belief in everything that must be believed in, of which the Messenger's message (ﷺ) is part, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We believe in Allah and in the Last Day﴾ [al-Baqarah: 8]. Thus in al-'Inayah.

(p-3088) The third: In singling out prayer and zakat for mention, there is glorification of their status and urging attention to them.

The fourth: The two verses indicate that the deeds of the disbelievers are nullified, having no reward in them.

And His saying, exalted is He:

The Explanation of His Words, exalted is He:

[19] ﴿Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims and the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque equal to one who believes in God and the Last Day and strives in the way of God? They are not equal in the sight of God. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

﴿Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims and the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque equal to one who believes in God and the Last Day and strives in the way of God? They are not equal in the sight of God. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

Al-'Awfi narrated in his Tafsir from Ibn 'Abbas that the polytheists said: "The maintenance of the House of God and the custody of the watering-place is better than one who believes and strives," and they used to boast of the Sacred Precinct and feel superior through it, because they were its people and its maintainers. So God preferred faith and striving alongside His Messenger over the polytheists' maintenance of the House and their custody of the watering-place, and He made clear that this does not benefit them along with polytheism, and that they are wrongdoers through their polytheism, and their maintenance avails them nothing.

The philologists said: (al-siqaya) with a kasra or a damma is the place of giving drink. In (al-Tahdhib): it is the place prepared for drink during the seasons and other times. End of quote.

In (al-Taj): "The siqayat al-hajj was what the Quraysh gave the pilgrims to drink, of raisin steeped in water, and al-'Abbas, may God be pleased with him, was in charge of it in the Jahiliyya and in Islam." End of quote.

Imam Muslim narrated from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: "I was beside the pulpit of the Prophet (ﷺ) when a man said: 'I do not care if I do no deed after Islam except to provide water for the pilgrims'; another said: 'Striving in the way of God is better than what you have said.' 'Umar rebuked them and said: 'Do not raise your voices beside the pulpit of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on Friday. But when I have prayed the Friday prayer, I will go in and ask him about what you have disputed.' Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims…﴾ the verse."

'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it in his (Musannaf), and its wording: "A man said: 'I do not care if I do no deed after Islam except to give the pilgrims water.' Another said: 'I do not care if I do no deed after Islam except to maintain the Sacred Mosque.' …" the hadith.

Some have said: The apparent meaning of this narration is that the comparison was between some Muslims who preferred providing water and maintenance over emigration and striving and their like, and the verse was revealed concerning that. Yet the earlier narration from Ibn 'Abbas contradicts this, as does the mention of faith on the side of the likened-to, and likewise the description of them as wrongdoers because of their equating.

I say: There is no contradiction. The apparent sense of the noble wording, according to what Ibn 'Abbas said, is beyond doubt. The statement of al-Nu'man, "then God revealed," means that a dialogue of this kind was addressed by a previously-established decisive verse, namely this verse, not that it was the cause of its revelation, as I have explained more than once.

This usage is common among the early scholars, and whoever does not perceive it will find the narrations contradicting one another and will be perplexed as to the resolution. So understand this and perceive it.

Abu al-Su'ud's support for its revelation concerning the Muslims, with what he extended on, is a heedlessness of the context and sequence of the verse, regarding the severe intimidation it thunders forth, and regarding what follows it of degrees of preference, and of restricting success, mercy and good pleasure to the likened-to.

A subtle point:

It is not hidden that siqaya and 'imara are both verbal nouns, which cannot be conceived as likened to physical entities, so there must be an elided noun on one side, i.e.: "Do you consider their people (the providers and maintainers) equal to one who believes in God…?" etc. This is supported by the reading of those who read (suqat al-hajj wa 'amarat al-masjid al-haram), or: "Do you consider them (the acts) like the faith of one who believes…?" etc.

Abu al-Baqa' said: The majority read (siqaya) with a ya', and the ya' is sound because it is followed by the feminine ta'.

Then, after explaining that they are not equal, the wrongdoing of the polytheists and their going astray, He, glorified is He, mentioned the ranks of the excellence of the believers, with His words:

(p-3090) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[20] ﴿Those who believed, emigrated, and strove in the cause of God with their wealth and their lives are greater in rank with God. And those are the triumphant.﴾

﴿Those who believed, emigrated, and strove in the cause of God with their wealth and their lives are greater in rank with God﴾ — i.e., than the people of the watering of the pilgrims (al-siqaya) and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque (al-'imara). Although they (those people) may have a rank with God, this was said according to their own supposition and claim. So said al-Alusi in (al-'Inaya) [i.e., Ibn al-Mulaqqin's/al-Hafnawi's glosses on the commentary; the text as given names al-'Inaya]. 

﴿And those are the triumphant﴾ — i.e., not you. That is: they are the ones specially singled out for success, to the exclusion of you.

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[21] ﴿Their Lord gives them good news of mercy from Him, and of His pleasure, and of gardens for them wherein is lasting bliss.﴾

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 9, verse 22:

The discussion of His, the Exalted's, saying:

[22] ﴿Abiding therein forever. Indeed, Allah has with Him a great reward.ﴩ

﴿Abiding therein forever. Indeed, Allah has with Him a great reward.﴾ Then the Exalted prohibited them from taking the polytheists as allies (muwalah), even if they were the nearest of kin, by His, glory be to Him, saying:

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[23] ﴿O you who believe, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies if they prefer disbelief over faith. And whoever among you takes them as allies, those are the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿O you who believe, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies⦆ That is: as intimate friends and confidants, to whom you disclose your secrets, whom you praise, and whom you defend. ﴿if they prefer⦆ That is: choose ﴿disbelief over faith. And whoever among you takes them as allies, those are the wrongdoers⦆ (p-3091) That is: because they have placed loyalty where it does not belong, and because they have transgressed and overstepped what Allah has commanded.

Then the Exalted indicated that the requirement of faith is to abandon the natural inclination when it becomes an obstacle to the love of Allah, the love of the means of reaching Him, and the love of what exalts His religion, by His saying:

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[24] ﴿Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your kinsfolk, the wealth you have acquired, the commerce you fear will decline, and the dwellings you are pleased with are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait until Allah brings His command. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.﴾

﴿Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, and your kinsfolk﴾ i.e., your closest relatives, or your tribe.

The lexicographers said: the 'ashirah (kinsfolk) of a man are the close paternal relatives of his father, or his tribe. It is like 'ashir, without the taa' marbuta, derived from the 'ishrah (companionship, i.e., association), meaning mu'ashara, because it is part of their dealings; or from the 'asharah (ten), which is the number of completeness, because it is a complete number. ﴿And wealth that you have acquired﴾ i.e., that you have earned. ﴿And commerce the decline of which you fear﴾ i.e., the passing of the time of its sale through your separation from it.

﴿And dwellings you are pleased with﴾ i.e., homes in which living pleases you, of houses and gardens. ﴿Are dearer to you than Allah﴾ i.e., the Bestower of everything; ﴿and His Messenger﴾, who is the intermediary of His blessings; ﴿and striving in His cause﴾ i.e., of that which exalts His religion. ﴿Then wait﴾ i.e., expect: ﴿until Allah brings His command﴾ i.e., His decree, which is either a swift punishment, or a deferred retribution, or the conquest of Makkah. This is a command of threat and intimidation. That is: await the subjugation of Allah, by claiming love for Him through faith, while belying that claim by preferring the love of other than Him. ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾ i.e., those who go outside obedience by allying with the polytheists, and who prefer the things mentioned over His pleasure, may He be exalted.

Notes:

The first: Some said: the fruit of the two verses is the prohibition of allying with disbelievers, even if they are relatives, and that this is a major sin, since it describes those who ally with them as wrongdoers, and the obligation of jihad, and preferring it over all these desired things enumerated, in obedience to Allah and His Messenger.

The second: al-Razi said: the second verse indicates that if a conflict arises between a single interest of the interests of the religion and all the important matters of this world, it becomes obligatory for the Muslim to prefer the religion over the world.

The third: In this verse there is a warning and a severe admonition, for hardly anyone is free from it; therefore it has been said that it is the most severe verse of reproach upon people, as expounded by al-Zamakhshari in al-Kashshaf with his words:

"This is a severe verse; you will not see one more severe than it. It seems to reproach people for the looseness of the bond of their religion and the instability of the cord of certainty. Let the most scrupulous and most pious of people be fair to himself: does he find in himself such steadfastness for the sake of Allah and firmness upon the religion of Allah that his religion is preferred over fathers, sons, siblings, kinsfolk, wealth, dwellings and all the portions of this world, and he strips himself of them for its sake? Or does Allah withhold from him the least of them for his benefit, so that he does not know which of his two sides is longer, and Satan misleads him away from the most exalted portion of the portions of religion, so that he is unconcerned, as if a fly had landed on his nose and he shooed it away?!"

And His saying, the Exalted:

The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 9, verse 25:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He:

[25] ﴿Indeed, Allah has given you victory in many battlefields and on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you, but it did not avail you at all, and the earth, spacious as it was, constricted for you, and you turned back in retreat.﴾

﴿Indeed, Allah has given you victory in many battlefields﴾ That is, in many battle positions and famous encounters, such as the Battle of Badr, Qurayzah, al-Nadir, al-Hudaybiyyah, Khaybar, and the Conquest of Makkah. The expeditions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as mentioned in the Two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn) on the authority of Zayd ibn Arqam, were nineteen expeditions (ghazwa). Buraydah added in a hadith: "He fought in eight of them." It is said that the total of his expeditions, detachments (sariyya), and dispatches (bu'uth) was seventy, and it was also said eighty. (p-3093)

﴿and on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you﴾ That is, you relied upon it, when you said: "We will not be defeated today because of small numbers." ﴿but it did not avail you at all﴾ That is, against the enemy's affair, despite their small number. ﴿and the earth, spacious as it was, constricted for you﴾ That is, with its breadth and vastness.

The "bi" (with) here indicates mulabasa (accompaniment, being attended by) and musahaba (companionship). That is, it constricted upon you while being spacious. This is an istiʿara tabaʿiyya (a derivative metaphor, a metaphor in which the verbal or descriptive element is borrowed), either because they could not find a place where they could settle in safety and tranquility due to the intensity of terror, or because they could not sit in one place, just as one cannot sit in a narrow place. ﴿then you turned back in retreat﴾ That is, defeated.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted:

[26] ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts you did not see, and He punished those who disbelieved. That is the recompense of the disbelievers.﴾

﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility﴾ That is, that by which you were calmed and steadied, [consisting of] His mercy and His help, the rout of the disbelievers, and the tranquility of hearts for the return to battle after the flight. ﴿upon His Messenger and upon the believers﴾ That is, those who had fled; the repetition of the preposition (ʿalā) serves to draw attention to the difference between their two states. Or [it refers to] those who stood firm with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and did not flee. Or [it refers to] all of them, and this is the most fitting.

There is no harm in affirming the root meaning of tranquility (sakīnah) in those who stood firm earlier, and in mentioning the attribute of faith to indicate that it is the cause of the sending down. Abu al-Suʿud conveyed this.

﴿and sent down hosts you did not see﴾ meaning the angels. ﴿and He punished those who disbelieved﴾ That is, by killing, capture, and taking captives. ﴿That is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾ for their disbelief in this world.

**On the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

[27] ﴿Then Allah turns in forgiveness after that to whom He wills. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿Then Allah turns in forgiveness after that to whom He wills﴾: that is, from among them, for a wisdom that requires it, meaning He grants them success in Islam. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving﴾: that is, He overlooks what has passed from them of disbelief and sins. ﴿Merciful﴾: that is, He bestows His favour upon them and rewards them.

**Notes (tanbihat, "points of attention"):**

**The first:** Regarding what is reported about the campaign (ghazwa, military expedition) of (Hunayn), also called the campaign of (Awtas). Both are places between Makkah and al-Ta'if, so the campaign was named after their location. It is also called the campaign of (Hawazin), because they were the ones who came to fight the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This event took place after the conquest of Makkah, in Shawwal of the eighth year after the Hijrah, for the conquest had occurred ten nights before the end of Ramadan. After it, "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained in Makkah for fifteen nights, shortening the prayer. Then he was informed that Hawazin and Thaqif had gathered against him, intending to march on Makkah, and they had camped at (Hunayn). When they heard of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) departure from Madinah, they thought that he was only coming to show them (his strength). Hawazin gathered around Malik ibn 'Awf of Banu Nasr, and with him came Banu Nasr ibn Mu'awiyah ibn Bakr ibn Hawazin, Banu Jusham ibn Mu'awiyah, Banu Sa'd ibn Bakr, some people of Banu Hilal ibn 'Amir ibn Sa'sa'ah ibn Mu'awiyah, the Ahlaf, and Banu Malik ibn Thaqif ibn Bakr, all of them.

Among Jusham was Duraid ibn al-Simmah, their leader and chief, an old shaykh who had nothing left but his judgement and his knowledge of war. He was brave and experienced, and the affairs of the people were all entrusted to Malik ibn 'Awf.

When it reached them that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had conquered Makkah, they set out intending to confront him. Malik resolved to march against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he drove with the people their wealth, their women and their children, believing that this would make them more steadfast in their position.
