(p-3127) ﴿And they were not commanded﴾, i.e., while those disbelievers were not commanded in their Book ﴿except to worship one God﴾, i.e., to obey His command and not to obey the command of another contrary to it. His words ﴿there is no deity except Him﴾ are a second attribute of ﴿God﴾, or a resumptive clause affirming monotheism. ﴿Exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾, i.e., in worship and obedience.

And His words, exalted is He:

The Explanation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[32] ﴿They wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refuses except to perfect His light, though the disbelievers dislike it.﴾

﴿They wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths﴾ — that is, they wish to quench His proof, which points to His oneness and His exaltedness above having offspring, or the Qur'an, or the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿But Allah refuses except to perfect His light﴾ — that is, by raising up monotheism and strengthening Islam. ﴿Though the disbelievers dislike it﴾ — that is, despite the evidences of monotheism.

The scholars of ma'ani (the science of meanings) said: "The light of Allah" is a primary explicit metaphor (isti'arah asliyyah tasrihiyyah) for His proof or what follows it, by likening each of them to light in its manifestness. "Extinguishing" is a complementary metaphor (tarshih). Or it is an allegorical metaphor (isti'arah tamthiliyyah), in which their condition in trying to nullify prophethood through denial is likened to the condition of one who seeks to extinguish a great light, spread across the horizons, which Allah wishes to increase by His breath.

Subtleties:

The first: Al-Shihab said: In each of the likened and the likened-to, excess and deficiency are observed, as he likened nullification to extinguishing with the mouth, and attributed the light to Allah. It is in the nature of a light attributed to Him that it be great, so how could it be extinguished by the blowing of a mouth? Yet there is a suitable relation between disbelief, which is concealment and the removal of manifestness, and extinguishing.

The second: It is not hidden that the words of Allah, Exalted, ﴿illa an yutimma﴾ ("except that He perfect") are an exceptive construction lacking its object (istithna' mufarragh), and it occupies the position of a direct object in the accusative. The lacking exception (istithna' mufarragh) occurs only after a negated verb, not an affirmative one, unless the meaning is sound.

Here, the lacking exception is valid after an affirmative: ﴿Allah refuses (wa-ya'ba Allah)﴾, because it is a negation in meaning, since it stands in opposition to ﴿they wish (yuridun)﴾. It contains an emphasis and an indication of refusal that is not present in the negation of wishing. That is: He does not will anything among things except the perfecting of His light; thus, its remaining as it was is included in what is excepted from, let alone its extinguishing. This was stated by Abu al-Su'ud.

Al-Zajjaj said: The item excepted from is omitted, its estimate being: (And Allah dislikes everything except the perfecting of His light).

Al-Shihab said: So the meaning is general, which validates the lacking exception in his view. Thus, there are two approaches among people regarding the justification of the lacking exception here.

The summary is that if what is intended is everything related to His light by the indication of context, then intending generality is valid, and the occurrence of the lacking exception with affirmative (established) matters is valid, as al-Zajjaj held, for there is no general term that has not been specified. Every generality is relative, yet it is sufficed with and called a generality.

Do you not see that their example, "I read except on such-and-such a day," has been estimated as every day, meaning the days of his life, not the days of time?

If the apparent form in such examples is considered, it is general and needs no negation. If the reality of the matter is considered, it is not general and is interpreted with negation. The meaning in both is one. It was interpreted as such here according to the one who held that interpretation, because the opposition requires it, for there is no affirmation that cannot be interpreted with negation; thus the lacking exception would apply to everything. This is not what Al-Radi stated.

For this reason it has been said: the lacking exception, though specific to negation, may nonetheless be inclined toward the meaning with the help of indicators and the suitability of contexts, so some affirmatives take the place of negatives in the validity of the lacking exception with them. This was also mentioned by al-Shihab.

The third: Abu al-Su'ud said: In the manifesting of "the light" (al-nur) in a place where a pronoun would be expected, attributed to His pronoun, Mighty and Majestic, there is an increase in attention to its matter and an honoring of it upon honor, and an indication of the cause of the ruling.

(p-3129) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[33] ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, even though the polytheists dislike it.﴾

﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, which is guidance for the God-fearing. ﴿And the religion of truth﴾, i.e., the firm monotheism that does not cease. ﴿That He may make it prevail﴾, i.e., the true religion, ﴿over all religion﴾, i.e., over all the other religions. ﴿Even though the polytheists dislike it﴾, i.e., dislike that this should be so.

The response (jawab) of "law" (even though) in both places is omitted, because what precedes it indicates it. The clause ﴿It is He who...﴾ and so on is an explanation and confirmation of the content of the clause before it, because the intended meaning of "completing His light" is making it prevail, and since it is, in its outcome, of the same meaning, He appended to it the same appendix. However, He expressed the disbelievers as "polytheists" to avoid the appearance of repetition, as stated in (al-'Inayah).

In the Sahih, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed God folded up the earth for me, its eastern and western parts, and the dominion of my community will reach what was folded up for me of it."

Imam Ahmad narrated from Mas'ud ibn Qabisa, or Qabisa ibn Mas'ud, who said: "This tribe of Muharib prayed the dawn prayer, and when they had prayed, a young man among them said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'Indeed the eastern and western parts of the earth will be opened to you, and its governors are in the Fire, except for those who fear God and fulfil the trust.'"

(p-3130) It was also narrated from Tamim al-Dari, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "This matter will certainly reach wherever the night and day reach, and God will not leave a house of adobe or of hair tent except that He will cause this religion to enter it, granting honour to the honourable and humiliation to the humiliated, an honour by which God honours Islam and a humiliation by which God humiliates disbelief."

Tamim al-Dari used to say: "I have known this in my own family: whoever among them embraced Islam attained good, nobility and honour, and whoever among them was a disbeliever attained humiliation, lowliness and the jizya."

It was also narrated from al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "There will not remain on the face of the earth a house of adobe or of hair tent except that the word of Islam will enter it, granting honour to the honourable and humiliation to the humiliated; either God will honour them and make them among its people, or He will humiliate them and they will submit to it."

It was also narrated from Adi ibn Hatim, who said: "I entered upon the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and he said: 'O Adi! Embrace Islam and you will be safe.' I said: I am of a religion. He said: 'I know your religion better than you do.' I said: You know my religion better than I do? He said: 'Yes. Are you not of the Rukusiyya, and do you not eat the quarter-share of your people?' I said: Yes! He said: 'Indeed this is not lawful for you in your religion.' He said: Hardly had he said it when I humbled myself before it. He said: 'Now, I know what it is that prevents you from Islam: you say, only the weak of the people follow him, and those who have no power, and the Arabs have cast them off. Do you know al-Hira?' I said: I have not seen it, but I have heard of it. He said: 'By Him in whose hand is my soul! (p-3131) God will surely complete this matter, until a woman riding in a litter will go out from al-Hira and circle the House without the protection of anyone, and the treasures of Kisra ibn Hurmuz will surely be conquered.' I said: Kisra ibn Hurmuz? He said: 'Yes! Kisra ibn Hurmuz, and wealth will be spent until no one accepts it.'"

Adi ibn Hatim said: "So this woman now goes out from al-Hira and circles the House without the protection of anyone. I was among those who conquered the treasures of Kisra ibn Hurmuz. By Him in whose hand is my soul, the third (matter) will certainly come to pass, for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) has said it."

Muslim narrated from A'isha, may God be pleased with her, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "The night and day will not pass until al-Lat and al-Uzza are worshipped." I said: O Messenger of God! Indeed I used to think, when God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth﴾ up to the verse, that this was complete! He said: "Indeed there will be from that what God, mighty and majestic, wills. Then God will send a pleasant wind, and every one in whose heart there is the weight of a mustard seed of faith will be taken, and there will remain those in whom there is no good, and they will return to the religion of their fathers."

Al-Alusi... [note: source says] In al-Lubab: the meaning of the verse is that the religion of Islam will certainly prevail over all religions, which is that God is not worshipped except by it.

Likewise it was narrated from Abu Hurayra, may God be pleased with him, that he said: This is a promise from God, exalted is He, that He will make Islam high above all religions, and the completion of this will only occur at the descent of Jesus.

Likewise al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: No one will remain except that he enters Islam.

Al-Shafi'i said: God has made the religion of His Messenger (ﷺ) prevail over all religions by clarifying to everyone who hears it that it is the truth and that what is beyond it of religions is falsehood; and He made it prevail over the polytheism of the People of the Book and the religion of the Unlettered, so the Messenger of God (ﷺ) overcame the Unlettered until they submitted to Islam, and some of them gave the jizya in humility, and his rule applied to them.

He said: This is its prevalence over all religion. End.

(p-3132) I say: What al-Shafi'i mentioned is one aspect of its prevalence, and the more precise is what preceded, that every sect will embrace it, for what the reform movements among the other creeds incline toward is now not far from Islam except slightly.

Then God, exalted is He, explained the state of the rabbis and monks in misleading their base followers, following the explanation of the bad condition of the followers in taking them as lords who are obeyed in commands and prohibitions and being followed in what they do and what they leave, with His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[34] ﴿O you who have believed, indeed many of the rabbis and the monks consume the wealth of people unjustly and avert [people] from the way of Allah. And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah - give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, indeed many of the rabbis and the monks consume the wealth of people unjustly﴾

That is: by the blameworthy means of bribery (rashā) in rulings, and by lightening and relaxing the laws (sharāʾiʿ) and other such things.

The word "consume" (al-akl) is a metaphor (majāz) for "taking" (al-akhdh), through a relation (ʿalāqa) of causality and effect, because taking is the greatest purpose of it. In this there is a condemnation of their state and a warning to the hearers against it that is not hidden. ﴿And avert [people] from the way of Allah﴾, that is, from the religion of Islam and its ruling, and from following the proofs, toward what they desire, or from the path established in the Torah and the Gospel, toward what they have invented and distorted.

Then he indicated that the cause of this is their preference for the love of wealth and its hoarding over the command of Allah, and their forgetting of His threat concerning hoarding, in His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾, that is, they guard them with the guarding of something buried in the earth. ﴿And do not spend it in the way of Allah﴾, that is, the way which is zakat (obligatory almsgiving). ﴿Then give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾

[p. 3133]

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

﴿On the Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell, and their forereheads, their sides, and their backs will be branded with it: "This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard."﴾

﴿On the Day when it will be heated﴾ means: it will be kindled. ﴿in the fire of Hell, and their foreheads, their sides, and their backs will be branded with it﴾. ﴿This is what you hoarded﴾ means: it will be said to them, in addition to what they are already suffering, "This is what you hoarded." ﴿for yourselves﴾ means: so that you might enjoy it. Thus it was the cause of their punishment. ﴿So taste what you used to hoard﴾ means: taste its evil consequence, which is its pain and its severity through branding.

In this verse there are several benefits.

The first: Some scholars said regarding His saying, exalted is He, ﴿they devour﴾, that it indicates the prohibition of bribery (rishwa) for falsehood. It has been narrated: "Allah has cursed the one who gives bribes and the one who takes them."

Similarly, it is prohibited to take a return for performing an obligatory act. Regarding the permissibility of giving (money) in order to reach one's right, there is a difference of opinion. (Some) preferred its permissibility in order to reach the right, like paying ransom to free a captive.

Al-Hakim said: The prohibition of bribery includes rulings, testimonies, legal opinions, the foundations of religion and its branches, and everyone who distorts anything for the sake of worldly gain. End.

The second: In the verse, as Ibn Kathir said, there is a warning against evil scholars and worshippers of error. As Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said: "Whoever among our scholars becomes corrupt has in him a resemblance to the Jews, and whoever among our worshippers becomes corrupt has in him a resemblance to the Christians."

In the authentic hadith: "You will surely follow the ways of those before you, step by step and exactly like the feather of an arrow with another feather." They said: "The Jews and the Christians?" He said: "Who else?" In another narration: "Persia and Rome?" He said: "And who are the people other than these?" Then he recited (a verse) by Ibn al-Mubarak:

"Has anything corrupted the religion except the kings, and the evil rabbis and their monks?"

The third: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿those who﴾ is the subject (mubtada'), and the predicate is ﴿hoard﴾ [al-Tawba: 34], or it is in the accusative with the implied meaning: "Give good tidings to those who hoard."

The definite article in the relative pronoun is for a specific reference (al-'ahd) and a known referent: either the rabbis and monks, or the Muslims who hoard, because the mention of the two groups has preceded, or it is something more general.

The first (view) was narrated from Mu'awiya, the second from al-Suddi, and the third from Ibn 'Abbas and Abu Dharr.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It is possible that the relative pronoun refers to the majority of the rabbis and monks, to indicate the combination of two blameworthy traits in them: taking bribes and hoarding wealth and withholding it from spending in the way of Allah.

It is also possible that what is meant is the Muslims who hoard and do not spend, and (the verse) links them with the bribe-takers among the Jews and Christians, as an intensification and an indication that whoever takes what is unlawful from them, and whoever among you does not give the good of his wealth, are equal in deserving the good tidings of painful punishment. End.

In al-Anwar (Al-Baydawi), it is said: The second (view) is supported by the fact that when (this verse) was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims, so 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, mentioned (this) to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: "Indeed Allah did not prescribe zakat except so that the rest of your wealth may be purified by it." Narrated by Abu Dawud and al-Hakim, who declared it authentic.

And the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whatever its zakat has been paid is not a hoard." Narrated by al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi. [p. 3135] That is: it is not the hoard that is threatened in the verse, for the threat concerning hoarding applies when one does not spend in what Allah has commanded to be spent.

As for his saying ﷺ: "Whoever leaves gold or silver (unpaid for), he will be branded with it," and similar (narrations), what is meant by them is the wealth whose due has not been paid, due to his saying ﷺ, in what al-Shaykhan (Al-Bukhari in his *Tarikh* and Muslim in his *Sahih*) narrated from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ: "There is no owner of gold or silver who does not pay its due, except that on the Day of Resurrection plates of fire will be made for him, and his side, his forehead, and his back will be branded with them." End.

The dispute between Mu'awiya and Abu Dharr concerning this verse is well known.

Al-Bukhari narrated from Zayd ibn Wahb who said: I passed by al-Rabadha, and there was Abu Dharr. I said: "What brought you to this place?" He said: "I was in Syria, and I disagreed with Mu'awiya concerning this verse: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾ [al-Tawba: 34]. Mu'awiya said: 'It was revealed concerning the People of the Book.' I said: 'It was revealed concerning us and them.' So there was some dispute between me and him in that. He wrote to 'Uthman complaining about me. 'Uthman wrote to me: 'Come to Medina.' So I came to it, and the people crowded around me as if they had never seen me before. I mentioned that to 'Uthman, and he said: 'If you wish, withdraw, and you would be near.'"

"That is what brought me to this place. Even if an Abyssinian slave were appointed over me, I would hear and obey."

In another narration by Ibn Jarir, after 'Uthman's saying to him, "Withdraw nearby," I said: "By Allah, I will not abandon what I was saying."

Abu Ya'la narrated that Abu Dharr used to say: "No dinar or dirham should remain overnight with any one of you, except what he spends in the way of Allah, or prepares for a creditor."

Mu'awiya wrote to 'Uthman: "If you have a need in Syria, send for Abu Dharr." 'Uthman wrote to him: "Come to me," and he came.

Ibn Kathir said: It was among the doctrines of Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, to prohibit storing what exceeds the sustenance of one's dependents. He used to issue legal opinions to that effect, urge them towards it, command them to it, and be stern in opposing it. Mu'awiya forbade him, but he did not desist.

So (Mu'awiya) feared that he would harm the people in this matter, and he wrote complaining about him to the Commander of the Believers 'Uthman, asking that he take him to him. 'Uthman summoned him to Medina, then settled him in al-Rabadha, and there he died, may Allah be pleased with him, during the caliphate of 'Uthman.

Mu'awiya, may Allah be pleased with him, tested him while he was with him, to see whether his action would agree with his words. He sent him a thousand dinars. He distributed them the same day. Then he sent to him the one who had brought them, saying: "Mu'awiya only sent me to someone other than you, and I made a mistake. So take back the gold."

He said: "Woe to you! It has already gone out. But when my wealth comes, we will settle accounts with you concerning it."

Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays said: I came to Medina, and while I was in a circle with a group of Quraysh, a man came, wearing coarse clothes, with a rough body and a rough face. He stood over them and said: "Give good tidings to the hoarders of a heated stone that will be heated in the fire of Hell. Then it will be placed on the nipple of one of them until it comes out from the top of his shoulder blade, and placed on his shoulder blade until it comes out from the nipple of his breast, and it will shake."

He said: The people lowered their heads, and I did not see any one of them respond to him with anything. He said: He turned away, and I followed him until he sat with Mu'awiya. I said: "I did not see these people except that they disliked what you said to them." He said: "These people do not know anything; they only gather the world." Narrated by Muslim, and al-Bukhari has something similar.

In the Sahih (it is recorded) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abu Dharr: "It would not please me that I had gold equal to Uhud, and three days would pass over me while I still had any of it, except a dinar that I set aside for a debt." [p. 3137]

Ibn Kathir said: "This, and Allah knows best, is what moved Abu Dharr to hold this view."

That is: and what al-Shaykhan also narrated from him: "I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was sitting in the shade of the Ka'ba. When he saw me, he said: 'They are the losers, by the Lord of the Ka'ba!' I said: 'What about them?' Then I came and sat, but I could not stay still, so I stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! May my father and mother be your ransom, who are they?' He said: 'They are the ones with the most wealth, except those who say such and such, and such and such, and such and such, before him, behind him, to his right and to his left, and they are few.'"

Imam Ahmad narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was with Abu Dharr when his stipend was paid out, and with him was a slave-girl who began to take care of his needs. Seven (dirhams) were left over with her, and he ordered her to buy copper coins with them.

He said: I said: "If only you had saved it for the need of your day, and for a guest who might come to you." He said: "My beloved (Prophet) bound me by a covenant that whatever gold or silver is tied up (stored), it becomes a burning coal for its owner until he spends it in the way of Allah, mighty and majestic, in full spending."

Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: Many reports from Abu Dharr have come down, indicating that he held the view that every accumulated wealth that exceeds the food and the adequate living is a hoard, and its doer is blamed, and that the verse of the threat was revealed concerning this. The majority of the Companions and those after them disagreed with him, and they applied the threat to those who withhold zakat. The most authentic thing they relied upon is the hadith of Talha and others concerning the story of the Bedouin, when he said: "Is there anything else incumbent upon me?" He said: "No, except that you volunteer." End.

[p. 3138] In summary, the majority hold that the blameworthy hoard is the wealth whose zakat has not been paid. Al-Bukhari titled a chapter in his *Sahih* accordingly, saying: "Chapter: Whatever its zakat has been paid is not a hoard."

It is supported by the hadith of Abu Hurayra, raised to the Prophet: "When you pay the zakat of your wealth, you have discharged what is upon you." Declared fair (hasan) by al-Tirmidhi and authentic by al-Hakim.

And from Ibn 'Umar: "Everything whose zakat has been paid, even if it is under seven earths, is not a hoard. And everything whose zakat is not paid is a hoard, even if it is apparent on the surface of the earth." Narrated by al-Bayhaqi as a marfu' report, then he said: "The well-known version is its being a mawquf (statement of a Companion)," like the hadith of Jabir: "When you pay the zakat of your wealth, you have removed its evil from you." Narrated by al-Hakim, and the preferred version is that it is mawquf.

Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them, and those who agreed with him, held that zakat abrogated the threat concerning hoarding.

Al-Bukhari narrated in his *Sahih* that a Bedouin said to Ibn 'Umar: "Inform me about the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾ [al-Tawba: 34], to the end of the verse." Ibn 'Umar said: "Whoever hoards it and does not pay its zakat, woe to him." This was before zakat was revealed. When it was revealed, Allah made it a purification for wealth.

Ibn Maja added: Then Ibn 'Umar said: "I would not care if I had gold equal to Uhud, knowing its count, that I would pay its zakat and use it in obedience to Allah, exalted is He."

Abu Dawud narrated it in the book *al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh* (Abrogating and Abrogated). This indicates that the threat concerns hoarding, which is withholding what exceeds the need from being used for mutual support. It was in the early period of Islam, then that was abrogated by the obligation of zakat, when Allah granted conquests and the zakat thresholds (nusub) were determined.

It also indicates [p. 3139] that the obligation of zakat was in the ninth year after the Hijra, and Ibn al-Athir in his *Tarikh* stated this decisively. Some strengthened it by what occurred in the lengthy story of Tha'laba ibn Hatib, in which: "When the verse of charity was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ sent an official, who said: 'This is nothing but jizya (poll tax), or the sister of jizya.'" And I say: It was made obligatory only in the ninth year.

And I say: This hadith has been declared weak by scholars, and the stronger point is that this surah in which this verse appears was revealed in the ninth year, as we have mentioned earlier. So when it was abrogated by zakat, zakat was in that year or after it, definitively.

Ibn Hajar said in *al-Fath*: The apparent view is that this was at the beginning of the matter, as previously transmitted from Ibn 'Umar. Ibn Battal cited as evidence for it His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They ask you what they should spend. Say: the surplus﴾ [al-Baqara: 219], meaning what exceeds sufficiency. So that was obligatory at the beginning, then it was abrogated, and Allah knows best.

In the Musnad, through the route of Ya'la ibn Shaddad ibn Aws, from his father, he said: Abu Dharr used to hear a hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that contained severity, then he would go out to his people, and then the Prophet ﷺ would grant a concession in it, but he would not accept the concession and would cling to the first command.

What we have cited regarding the view of Abu Dharr is what the exegetes and commentators of hadith have related.

Some people claimed that what moved Abu Dharr to this was his witnessing Mu'awiya's appropriation of the fay' (spoils that came without fighting). The established fact is that the rightly-guided Caliphs, may Allah be pleased with them, used to regard the fay' as belonging to all Muslims, equally among fighters and others. Perhaps this is because fighting is an obligation on all Muslims, so all of them fall under that ruling.

He said: What supports that this applies to all Muslims is that Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), when he was in al-Sham, where the governor on behalf of the caliph Uthman was Mu'awiyah (may Allah be pleased with both of them), saw from Mu'awiyah what indicated his eagerness to hoard wealth in the treasury (bayt al-mal), to spend it on the public interests he saw for the Muslims. Abu Dharr was known for scrupulousness (wara') and was very keen to protect the rights of the Muslims, speaking the truth even against himself.

He began to speak about this matter among the people, and he gathered for himself a faction from the people of al-Sham to help him demand that Mu'awiyah return the wealth to the Muslims, and to declare that there was no acceptance of its being hoarded in the treasury under any circumstances, except for distributing it among all Muslims, since they all share in what Allah has bestowed upon them. Many people followed him in this view, gathering for this purpose secretly and openly, until it nearly became a fitnah (strife). So Mu'awiyah complained of him to the caliph Uthman (may Allah be pleased with them all), and he banished him to al-Rabadhah, out of fear of what might happen that would have an unpraised outcome. End of quotation.

Ibn Hajar also transmitted something close to this in al-Fath, where he said: The correct view is that Abu Dharr's denunciation was directed at the rulers who take the wealth for themselves and do not spend it in its proper way.

Fourth: The pronoun is said in the feminine form in ﴿ولا يُنْفِقُونَها﴾ [al-Tawbah: 34], although the apparent form would be the dual, since two things are mentioned, because what is meant by them is abundant dinars and dirhams. This is because the abundant amount of them is what constitutes a hoard (kanz), so he used the plural pronoun to indicate abundance; had he used the dual, it would have allowed a different meaning. It is also said that the pronoun refers to the hoards (kunuz) or the wealth understood from the context, so the ruling is general, and for this reason it departs from the apparent form. Mentioning the two specifically is because they are the predominant basic form of wealth, for specification.

It is also said that the pronoun refers to silver, and it was sufficient with it, because it is more abundant and people are more in need of it, and because gold is understood from it by priority, while being close to it in wording.

Fifth: In His saying, Exalted is He, (فَبَشِّرْهم) [so give them good tidings], there is mockery of them, as in the line:
"Their greeting among them is a painful blow."
It is also said: glad tidings (bishara) is news that changes the color of the skin (bashara) due to its effect on the heart, whether it comes from joy or from grief.

Sixth: It has been said regarding specifying these three parts of the body for branding, rather than others, that gathering them and withholding wealth was in pursuit of prestige through wealth and enjoying luxurious foods and fine clothing. So for their prominence and their well-known leadership, their faces were branded, and because their sides were filled with food, their sides were branded, and because of what they wore on their backs, their backs were branded.

It is also said: because when a poor person asks them, signs of aversion and refusal appear on them, so their faces frown and contract. Then, if he repeats the request, they turn away from him and leave him aside, and then if he persists, they turn their backs to him and face another direction. This is the utmost in rejection and the extreme in refusal, indicating dislike of giving and bestowing.

This is the practice of those who withhold goodness and kindness, and the habit of the miserly, so this was the cause for branding these parts. It is also said: because these parts are the noblest of the outward organs, since they contain the principal organs, which are the brain, the heart, and the liver; or because they are the origins of the four directions, which are the front, back, and two sides of the body, so it is a metonymy for the whole body.

Al-Qashani said: gathering wealth and hoarding it without spending it occurs only from the entrenchment of the vice of stinginess and love of wealth, and every vice has a branding by which its possessor is tormented in the Hereafter and disgraced in this world. Since the material from which this vice takes root and becomes firmly established is that wealth, and since it is what is heated in the fire of the blazing nature and the abyss of desire, he is branded with it.

These organs were specified because stinginess is embedded in the soul, and the soul overcomes the heart from these directions, not from the upper direction, which is the direction of the spirit's dominance and the passage of truths and lights, nor from the lower direction, which is of the corporeal nature, since nature cannot take hold there; so the remaining directions are left, and he is harmed and tormented from the four directions, just as you see him being blamed for them in this world. He is also repaid from these directions: either he is confronted with them openly and disgraced, or he is secretly insulted at his side, or he is slandered behind his back. End of quotation.

Seventh: Abu al-Baqa said: (يَوْمَ) in His saying, ﴿يَوْمَ يُحْمى عَلَيْها﴾ [on the Day it will be heated], is a temporal adverb in meaning, i.e., He will punish them on that day.

It is also said: its estimated form is "the torment of a day," and "torment" is a substitute for the first, and when the noun was omitted, "the day" took its place. It is also said: the estimate is "remember," and (عَلَيْها) is in the place of nominative case, as it stands in for the subject.

It is also said: the substitute for the subject is a hidden pronoun, i.e., the fuel or the embers will be heated, and (بِها) means with the hoards. It is also said that it means (فِيها), i.e., in Hell. It is also said: (يَوْمَ) is an adverb of an omitted verb, its estimate being: "On the day it will be heated, it will be said to them: This is what you hoarded."

When, earlier, Exalted is He explained the boldness of the rabbis and monks in altering the rulings of Allah, preferring their own interests, He followed it with what the polytheists dared to do in a similar matter, changing the sacred months that Allah has made sacred into other months, namely the postponement (nasi') that follows, also out of adherence to their desires. He thus reproached them for their effort to alter the reckoning of the year according to their whims and opinions, which increased their disbelief. So He, glorified is He, said:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[36] ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah, the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them four are sacred. That is the correct religion. So do not wrong yourselves therein. And fight against the polytheists all together as they fight against you all together. And know that Allah is with those who fear Him.﴾

﴿Indeed, the number of months﴾, i.e., their count, ﴿with Allah﴾, i.e., in His ruling, ﴿is twelve months﴾, which are the lunar months upon which the orbit of the legal rulings (aḥkām shar'iyya) revolves, ﴿in the Book of Allah﴾, i.e., in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawḥ al-maḥfūẓ), or in what He has established and made obligatory from His ruling.

His saying ﴿the day He created the heavens and the earth﴾ is linked to what is contained in the prepositional phrase (al-jār wa-al-majrūr) of the sense of "being established" (al-istiqrār). He intended by "the Book" that it is a verbal noun (maṣdar), and the meaning is: this matter is established in itself (fī nafs al-amr), since Allah Exalted created the bodies, the movements and the times. This was reported by Abu al-Su'ud.

﴿Of them﴾, i.e., of those twelve months, ﴿four are sacred﴾: three are consecutive (sard): Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and al-Muharram; and one is solitary (fard), which is Rajab. ﴿That﴾, i.e., the sanctity of the four mentioned months, ﴿is the correct religion﴾, i.e., the upright one. ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾, i.e., by violating their sanctity through fighting in them.

Ibn Ishaq said: i.e., do not make their sacred [status] permissible, nor make their permissible [status] sacred, as the people of polytheism did. ﴿And fight against the polytheists all together﴾, i.e., all of them, ﴿as they fight against you all together﴾. ﴿And know that Allah is with those who fear Him﴾, i.e., with support and assistance.

Then Exalted Allah clarified the fruit of this introduction, which is the prohibition of altering what has been designated as sacred among the sacred months, and the obligation to adhere to them as prescribed in His Book, censuring the polytheists for their disbelief in neglecting that, by His saying, glorified is He:

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[ 37 ] ﴿Indeed, the postponement (al-nasi') is an increase in disbelief. Those who disbelieve are led astray by it. They make it lawful one year and make it unlawful another year, so that they may conform to the number of what Allah has made sacred, and thus make lawful what Allah has made unlawful. The evil of their deeds has been made attractive to them. And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾

﴿Indeed, the postponement (al-nasi')﴾, that is, the postponing of the sanctity of one month to another month. It is a verbal noun from "nasa'ahu" (he postponed it) when he delays it. ﴿is an increase in disbelief﴾, because it is making lawful what Allah has made unlawful and making unlawful what He has made lawful. So it is another disbelief added to their disbelief. ﴿Those who disbelieve are led astray by it﴾, that is, they are led astray from Allah's rulings, since they combine the lawfulness and the sanctity within a single month. ﴿They make it lawful one year﴾, that is, they make the postponed month, from among the sacred months, lawful for one year, and make another month in its place unlawful.

﴿And make it unlawful another year﴾, that is, they leave it in its original sanctity and observe it for another year, when no purpose of theirs is tied to changing it. The expression of that as "making unlawful" is in consideration of their having made it lawful in the previous year. The two clauses are an explanation of the "going astray", or they are in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal).

Al-Zamakhshari said: "The nasi' is the postponement of the sanctity of a month to another month. That is because they were people of wars and raids. When the sacred month came while they were fighting, it was hard for them to abandon fighting, so they would make it lawful [p. 3144] and make unlawful another month in its place, until they abandoned specifying the sacred months with sanctity. They would make unlawful four months from the hardest months of the year. This is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿so that they may conform to the number of what Allah has made sacred﴾, that is, so that they may match the number, which is four, and not contradict it. They contradicted the specification, which is one of the two obligations. Perhaps they would also add to the number of months, making them thirteen or fourteen, so that the time would be wide enough for them."

For this reason, He, Mighty and Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months﴾ [al-Tawbah: 36], meaning without any addition they had introduced. ﴿So that they make lawful what Allah has made unlawful﴾ by abandoning the specification of the months by their particular identity. ﴿The evil of their deeds has been made attractive to them﴾, so they believed their ugliness to be good. ﴿And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾

Know that in these two verses there are several issues.

The first: the rulings are tied to the Arab months, which are the months of the crescent moons, not the solar months.

It is said that the first of the lunar months was made to be Muharram, which occurred in the time of 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. Before that, dating was by the Year of the Elephant. Then in the early period of Islam it was dated from Rabi' al-Awwal.

Ibn Kathir here transmitted from al-Sakhawi the aspects of the naming of the months by which they were named. We will present that, narrated from the authoritative mother-sources of the language on which reliance is placed, so we say:

1 - Muharram: as a passive participle, it is the first of the Arab months. They attached the definite article "al" to it, hinting at its original adjectival character, and made it a proper name through both, like al-najm and al-Dabaran and similar. It is not permitted for the article to be attached to any other month according to some, while according to others it is permitted with Safar and Shawwal.

The plural of Muharram is muharramat. Muharram is the "month of Allah." The Arabs named it with this name because they did not make fighting lawful in it. It was attributed to Allah, Exalted is He, as a way of magnifying it, just as the Ka'bah was called "the House of Allah." It is also said that it was named so because it is one of the sacred months. Ibn Sida said: "This is not strong."

2 - Safar: the month that comes after Muharram. Some said: it was named so because they would obtain food in it from places. It is also said: because Makkah would become empty (yusfir) of its people when they traveled. It was narrated from Ru'bah that he said: "They named the month Safar because they would raid the tribes in it, leaving those they met empty (sifr) of goods." This is because Safar comes after Muharram, and they said: "The people became empty (safira) of us, emptiness (safaran)." Tha'lab said: "All people treat Safar as diptote, except Abu 'Ubaydah, who made it indeclinable for being a proper noun and feminine, with the intention of the hour, meaning that all times are hours." When they combine it with Muharram they say: "Safarayn." From this is the saying of Abu Dhu'ayb:

"They stayed in it like the stay of the bent (al-hanīf) between the two months of Jumada and the two months of Safar."

(It was cited in the Lisan in the root ṣ-f-r, and it is not in the Diwan of the Hudhaliyyin.)

Ibn Durayd said: "The two Safars are two months of the year. One of them was named Muharram in Islam. Its plural is asfar, like sabab and asbab. Sometimes it is said safarat."

3 and 4 - Rabi': two months after Safar. They were named so because they were marked (hudda) in this time, so it became attached to them at other times. They say: "Only Rabi' al-Awwal and Rabi' al-Akhir may be said of them," with the addition of "month" (shahr) and the nunation of "Rabi'", and making "al-Awwal" and "al-Akhir" an attributive adjective following in case. It is also permitted to use the construct form. It is, according to some, an instance of a thing being attributed to itself, due to the difference of the two words, like: ﴿and the grain of the harvest﴾ [Qaf: 9], ﴿and the abode of the Hereafter﴾ [al-Nahl: 30], ﴿the sure truth of certainty﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 95], and "the masjid of the mosque." Some said: The Arabs obligatorily used the word "shahr" before "Rabi'," because the word "Rabi'" is shared between the month and the season. So they kept the word "shahr" for the month and omitted it for the season, for the sake of distinction.

Al-Azhari also said: "The Arabs mention all the months unaccompanied by the word 'shahr' except the two months of Rabi' and Ramadan."

The month may be made dual and plural, so one says: shahra Rabi' (the two months of Rabi'), ashhur Rabi' and shuhur Rabi'.

5 and 6 - Jumada al-Ula and al-Akhira (like Hubara): the two months following the two months of Rabi'. Jumada is a feminine definite noun. Ibn al-Anbari said: "All the names of the months are masculine, except the two Jumadas, which are feminine. You say: 'Jumada passed with what was in it.'" The poet said:

"When Jumada withholds its rain,
my gardens are adorned with a watered, reed-cut pasture."

Then he said: "If the masculine form of Jumada appears in poetry, it is a going to the meaning of the month, as they say: 'This is a thousand dirhams,' meaning: 'These are the dirhams.'"

Its plural following its form is jumadiyyat. Al-Ula and al-Akhira are adjectives of it, so al-Akhira is in the sense of "the later one."

They said: "One does not say Jumada al-Ukhra, because al-Ukhra means 'the other one,' which covers both the earlier and the later, so confusion would result. Therefore it is said al-Akhira, to be specific to the later one." It was named so because of the freezing (jumud) of water in it, at the time the months were named, due to the cold. He said:

"On a night of Jumada, full of dews,
the dog cannot see the tent-cord in its darkness.
The dog does not bark in it even once,
until it wraps its tail around its snout."

7 - Rajab: it was named so for their magnifying it in the Jahiliyyah, abstaining from fighting in it. It is said: "Rajaba fulanan," meaning he feared him and magnified him, like rajjabahu. It is triptote (munsarif) and has plurals: arjab, arjibah, arjub, rijab, rujub, araajib, araajib and rajabanat.

When they combine Sha'ban with it, they say "Rajabani," by way of predominance (taghlib).

In the hadith: "Rajab of Mudar, which is between Jumada and Sha'ban." The phrase "between Jumada and Sha'ban" is an emphasis of the matter and clarification, because they used to postpone it from month to month, so it would shift from its place which is specific to it. So he made clear to them that it is the month between Jumada and Sha'ban, not what they called it according to the reckoning of the postponement. It was said "Rajab of Mudar" and attributed to them, because they were more magnifying of it than others, as if they were specially associated with it. Some of them mentioned seventeen names for it.

8 - Sha'ban: its plural is sha'banat and sha'abin, from "tasha''aba" when it disperses. They would disperse in it in search of water, and it is said: in raids.

Tha'lab said: some said: Sha'ban was named so because it "sha'aba," that is, it appeared between the month of Ramadan and Rajab.

9 - Ramadan: it was named so because its placement coincided with the ramad (with two fatha), which is intense heat. Its plurals are ramadanat and armida'. From Yunus it is heard as ramadin, like sha'abin. It is also said that it derives from "ramida al-sa'im yarmadu," when the heat of the inside of the fasting person intensifies from the intensity of thirst. This is the view of al-Farra'.

Some scholars said: It is disliked to say "Ramadan came" and the like when the month is intended, with no indicator to show it. Rather one says: "The month of Ramadan came." He used as evidence the hadith: "Do not say 'Ramadan,' for Ramadan is one of the names of Allah, Exalted is He, but say 'the month of Ramadan.'" This hadith was weakened by al-Bayhaqi, and its weakness is evident, because no scholar has been reported to have said that Ramadan is one of the names of Allah, Exalted is He, so it is not acted upon.

The apparent view is that it is permissible without disliking it, as al-Bukhari and a group of verifiers held, because nothing authentic has been established regarding its being disliked.

Authentic hadiths have established what indicates permissibility absolutely, such as his saying: "When Ramadan comes, the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of Hellfire are closed, and the devils are chained."

Al-Suhayli verified that omitting "shahr" has a position that differs from the position of mentioning it, which the eloquent speaker takes into account.

Its summary: in omitting it there is an indication of generality, and in mentioning it there is the opposite of that. For when you say "the month of such-and-such," it becomes a time-frame and the generality disappears from the expression, since the meaning is "in the month." For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever fasts Ramadan," and did not say "the month of Ramadan," so that the action would apply to all of it. End of quote. So let it be considered.

10 - Shawwal: the month of Eid al-Fitr, and the first of the months of Hajj. Its plural is shawwalat and shawawil, and the definite article may be attached to it.

Ibn Faris said: "Some claimed that Shawwal was named so because it coincided with a time when camels raise (tashul) their tails, that is, they lift their tails for mating. This is the view of al-Farra'."

Others said: it was named for the "tashwil" (lifting) of camels' milk, which is its turning away and decline, and likewise the state of camels in the intensity of heat and the cutting off of fresh pasture. The Arabs used to consider it a bad omen to conclude marriage contracts in it, saying: the woman being married would refuse her husband until the camel mounted by the stallion is refused when she conceives and raises her tail. So the Prophet (ﷺ) nullified their bad omen. "'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married me in Shawwal, and consummated the marriage with me in Shawwal. Which of his wives was more favored by him than me?'"

11 - Dhu al-Qa'dah: with fatha or kasra on the qaf being a dialect. It was named so because the Arabs would sit (yaq'udun) in it, abstaining from journeys, raiding, seeking provisions and searching for pasture, and would perform Hajj in Dhu al-Hijjah. The plural is dhawat al-qa'dah and dhawat al-qa'adat, and the dual is dhawata al-qa'dah and dhawata al-qa'datayn, so they made both words dual and plural. This is rare, because the two words are like one word, and no single word takes both the dual and plural markers.

12 - Dhu al-Hijjah: the month in which Hajj occurs. It was named so for the Hajj in it. The plural is dhawat al-hijjah, and they did not say "dhawu" for its singular. The fatha is more common in it than the kasra. Al-hijjah with kasra means one single instance of Hajj, and this is anomalous, because the analogy for a single instance is fatha, end of quote.

We have presented this in summary from al-Misbah, al-Qamus and its commentary.

The second issue: we previously mentioned that the four sacred months are three consecutive (sard), meaning in succession, and one single (fard). [p. 3149] The Arabs did not make fighting lawful in them, except two tribes: Khath'am and Tayy', for they would make the months lawful. Those who postponed the months during the season would say: "We have made fighting unlawful for you in these months, except the blood of those who make it lawful," so the Arabs would make their blood lawful specifically in these months.

For a group of Ghatafan and Qays, called the Habba'at, there were eight sacred months, called al-Basl, which they made unlawful out of severity and excess.

The third issue: Ibn Kathir said: The sacred months were four: three consecutive and one single, for the sake of performing the rites of Hajj and Umrah. So one month before the months of Hajj was made sacred, namely Dhu al-Qa'dah, because they would sit in it from fighting, and the month of Dhu al-Hijjah was made sacred, because in it they would perform Hajj and be occupied with the rites.

وحُرِّمَ بَعْدَهُ شَهْرٌ آخَرُ، وهو المُحَرَّمُ، لِيَرْجِعُوا فِيهِ إلى أقْصى بِلادِهِمْ آمِنِينَ. وحُرِّمَ رَجَبٌ في وسَطِ الحَوْلِ، لِأجْلِ زِيارَةِ البَيْتِ والِاعْتِمارِ بِهِ، لِمَن يَقْدَمُ إلَيْهِ مِن أقْصى جَزِيرَةِ العَرَبِ، فَيَزُورُهُ ثُمَّ يَعُودُ إلى وطَنِهِ فِيهِ آمِنًا.

الرّابِعَةُ: قالَ النَّوَوِيُّ في (" شَرْحِ مُسْلِمٍ "): وقَدِ اخْتَلَفُوا في كَيْفِيَّةِ عِدَّتِها عَلى قَوْلَيْنِ، حَكاهُما الإمامُ أبُو جَعْفَرٍ النَّحّاسُ في كِتابِهِ (" صِناعَةِ الكاتِبِ ")، قالَ: ذَهَبَ الكُوفِيُّونَ إلى أنَّهُ يُقالُ: المُحَرَّمُ ورَجَبٌ وذُو القِعْدَةِ وذُو الحِجَّةِ. قالَ: والكُتّابُ يَمِيلُونَ إلى هَذا القَوْلِ، لِيَأْتُوا بِهِنَّ مِن سَنَةٍ واحِدَةٍ. قالَ: وأهْلُ المَدِينَةِ يَقُولُونَ: ذُو القِعْدَةِ وذُو الحِجَّةِ والمُحَرَّمُ ورَجَبٌ، وقَوْمٌ يُنْكِرُونَ هَذا ويَقُولُونَ: جاءُوا بِهِنَّ مِن سَنَتَيْنِ.

قالَ أبُو جَعْفَرٍ: وهَذا غَلَطٌ بَيِّنٌ، وجَهْلٌ بِاللُّغَةِ، لِأنَّهُ قَدْ عُلِمَ المُرادُ، وأنَّ المَقْصُودَ ذِكْرُهُ، وأنَّها في كُلِّ سَنَةٍ، فَكَيْفَ يُتَوَهَّمُ أنَّها مِن سَنَتَيْنِ؟ قالَ: والأوْلى والِاخْتِيارُ ما قالَهُ أهْلُ المَدِينَةِ، لِأنَّ الأخْبارَ قَدْ تَظاهَرَتْ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) كَما قالُوا، مِن رِوايَةِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ وأبِي هُرَيْرَةَ وأبِي بَكْرَةَ (رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهم)، قالَ: وهَذا أيْضًا قَوْلُ أكْثَرِ أهْلِ التَّأْوِيلِ (ta'wil: التفسير وبيان المراد).

الخامِسَةُ: اسْتَنْبَطَ بَعْضُهم مِن قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿فَلا تَظْلِمُوا فِيهِنَّ أنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ (سورة التوبة: ٣٦) أنَّ الإثْمَ (p-٣١٥٠) فِي هَذِهِ الأشْهُرِ المُحَرَّمَةِ آكَدُ وأبْلَغُ مِنْهُ في غَيْرِها، كَما أنَّ المَعاصِيَ في البَلَدِ الحَرامِ تُضاعَفُ، لِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿ومَن يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإلْحادٍ بِظُلْمٍ نُذِقْهُ مِن عَذابٍ ألِيمٍ﴾ (سورة الحج: ٢٥). وكَذَلِكَ الشَّهْرُ الحَرامُ تَغْلُظُ فِيهِ الآثامُ، ولِهَذا تَغْلُظُ فِيهِ الدِّيَةُ في مَذْهَبِ الشّافِعِيِّ وطائِفَةٍ كَثِيرَةٍ مِنَ العُلَماءِ، وكَذا في حَقِّ مَن قَتَلَ في الحَرَمِ أوْ قَتَلَ ذا مُحَرَّمٍ.

وقالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ فِيما رَواهُ عَنْهُ عَلِيُّ بْنُ أبِي طَلْحَةَ: أنَّهُ تَعالى اخْتَصَّ مِنَ الأشْهُرِ أرْبَعَةَ أشْهُرٍ جَعَلَهُنَّ حَرامًا، وعَظَّمَ حُرُماتِهِنَّ، وجَعَلَ الذَّنْبَ فِيهِنَّ أعْظَمَ، والعَمَلَ الصّالِحَ والأجْرَ أعْظَمَ.

وقالَ قَتادَةُ: إنَّ الظُّلْمَ في الأشْهُرِ الحُرُمِ أعْظَمُ خَطِيئَةً ووِزْرًا مِنَ الظُّلْمِ فِيما سِواها، وإنْ كانَ الظُّلْمُ عَلى كُلِّ حالٍ عَظِيمًا، ولَكِنَّ اللَّهَ يُعَظِّمُ مِن أمْرِهِ ما يَشاءُ. وقالَ: إنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفى صَفايا مِن خَلْقِهِ، اصْطَفى مِنَ المَلائِكَةِ رُسُلًا، ومِنَ النّاسِ رُسُلًا، واصْطَفى مِنَ الكَلامِ ذِكْرَهُ، واصْطَفى مِنَ الأرْضِ المَساجِدَ، واصْطَفى مِنَ الشُّهُورِ رَمَضانَ والأشْهُرَ الحُرُمَ، واصْطَفى مِنَ الأيّامِ يَوْمَ الجُمُعَةِ، واصْطَفى مِنَ اللَّيالِي لَيْلَةَ القَدْرِ، فَعَظِّمُوا ما عَظَّمَ اللَّهُ، فَإنَّما تَعْظِيمُ الأُمُورِ بِما عَظَّمَ اللَّهُ بِهِ عِنْدَ أهْلِ الفَهْمِ، وأهْلِ العَقْلِ. (نَقَلَهُ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ). ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ: أنَّ ابْنَ جَرِيرٍ اخْتارَ في قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿فَلا تَظْلِمُوا فِيهِنَّ أنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ (سورة التوبة: ٣٦) ما قالَهُ ابْنُ إسْحاقَ فِيما تَقَدَّمَ.

أقُولُ: هو الظّاهِرُ المُتَبادِرُ.

السّادِسَةُ: قالَ المَهايِمِيُّ: إنَّما كانَ مِنها أرْبَعَةٌ حُرُمٌ، لِيَكُونَ ثُلْثُ السُّنَّةِ تَغْلِيبًا لِلتَّحْلِيلِ الَّذِي هو مُقْتَضى سِعَةِ الرَّحْمَةِ، عَلى التَّحْرِيمِ الَّذِي هو مُقْتَضى الغَضَبِ، فَجُعِلَ أوَّلُ السَّنَةِ وآخِرُها، وهو المُحَرَّمُ وذُو الحِجَّةِ، ولَمّا لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ وسَطٌ صَحِيحٌ، أُخِذَ أوَّلُ النِّصْفِ الآخَرِ، وهو رَجَبٌ، فَبَقِيَ مِنَ الثُّلُثِ شَهْرٌ، فَأُخِذَ قَبْلَ الآخَرِ، وهو ذُو القِعْدَةِ، لِيَكُونَ مَعَ آخِرِ السَّنَةِ المُتَّصِلَةِ بِأوَّلِها وِتْرًا، وبَقِيَ وِتْرِيَّةُ رَجَبٍ، فَتَتِمُّ السَّنَةُ عَلى التَّحْرِيمِ بِاعْتِبارِ أوَّلِها وآخِرِها وأوْسَطِها، مَعَ تَذَكُّرِ وِتْرِيَّةِ الحَقِّ المُؤَكِّدِ لِلتَّحْرِيمِ.
انْتَهى.

(p-٣١٥١) السّابِعَةُ: اسْتَدَلَّ جَماعَةٌ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿فَلا تَظْلِمُوا فِيهِنَّ أنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ (سورة التوبة: ٣٦) عَلى أنَّ تَحْرِيمَ القِتالِ في الأشْهُرِ الحُرُمِ ثابِتٌ مُحْكَمٌ لَمْ يُنْسَخْ (naskh: النسخ، أي رفع حكم شرعي بدليل متأخر)، وكَذا بِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُحِلُّوا شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ ولا الشَّهْرَ الحَرامَ﴾ (سورة المائدة: ٢)، وبِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿فَإذا انْسَلَخَ الأشْهُرُ الحُرُمُ فاقْتُلُوا المُشْرِكِينَ﴾ (سورة التوبة: ٥) الآيَةَ.

وذَهَبَ آخَرُونَ إلى أنَّ تَحْرِيمَ القِتالِ فِيها مَنسُوخٌ بِآيَةِ السَّيْفِ، يَعْنِي قَوْلَهُ تَعالى: ﴿وقاتِلُوا المُشْرِكِينَ كافَّةً﴾ (سورة التوبة: ٣٦). قالُوا: ظاهِرُ السِّياقِ مُشْعِرٌ بِأنَّهُ أمَرَ بِذَلِكَ أمْرًا عامًّا في الشَّهْرِ الحَرامِ، لَأوْشَكَ أنْ يُقَيِّدَهُ بِانْسِلاخِها، وبِأنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) حاصَرَ أهْلَ الطّائِفِ في شَهْرٍ حَرامٍ، وهو ذُو القِعْدَةِ، كَما ثَبَتَ في الصَّحِيحَيْنِ، أنَّهُ خَرَجَ إلى هَوازِنَ في شَوّالٍ، فَما كَسَرَهم واسْتَفاءَ أمْوالَهم ورَجَعَ فَلُّهم، لَجَؤُوا إلى الطّائِفِ، فَعَمَدَ إلى الطّائِفِ فَحاصَرَهم أرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا، وانْصَرَفَ ولَمْ يَفْتَتِحْها، فَثَبَتَ أنَّهُ حاصَرَ في الشَّهْرِ الحَرامِ.

وأجابَ الأوَّلُونَ بِأنَّ الأمْرَ بِقَتْلِ المُشْرِكِينَ ومُقاتَلَتِهِمْ مُقَيَّدٌ بِانْسِلاخِ الأشْهُرِ الحُرُمِ، كَما في قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿فَإذا انْسَلَخَ الأشْهُرُ الحُرُمُ﴾ (سورة التوبة: ٥) الآيَةَ، فَتَكُونُ سائِرُ الآياتِ المُتَضَمِّنَةِ لِلْأمْرِ بِالقِتالِ مُفِيدَةً بِما وَرَدَ في تَحْرِيمِ القِتالِ في الأشْهُرِ الحُرُمِ، كَما هي مُقَيَّدَةٌ بِتَحْرِيمِ القِتالِ في الحَرَمِ، لِلْأدِلَّةِ الوارِدَةِ في تَحْرِيمِ القِتالِ فِيهِ. فَقَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وقاتِلُوا المُشْرِكِينَ كافَّةً﴾ (سورة التوبة: ٣٦) الآيَةَ، مِن بابِ التَّهْيِيجِ والتَّحْضِيضِ، أيْ: كَما يَجْتَمِعُونَ لِحَرْبِكم إذا حارَبُوكم، فاجْتَمِعُوا كَذَلِكَ لَهم، أوْ هو إذْنٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِقِتالِ المُشْرِكِينَ في الشَّهْرِ الحَرامِ، إذا كانَتِ البُداءَةُ مِنهم، كَما قالَ تَعالى: ﴿الشَّهْرُ الحَرامُ بِالشَّهْرِ الحَرامِ والحُرُماتُ قِصاصٌ﴾ (سورة البقرة: ١٩٤)، وقالَ تَعالى: ﴿ولا تُقاتِلُوهم عِنْدَ المَسْجِدِ الحَرامِ حَتّى يُقاتِلُوكم فِيهِ فَإنْ قاتَلُوكم فاقْتُلُوهُمْ﴾ (سورة البقرة: ١٩١) الآيَةَ _. (p-٣١٥٢) وهَكَذا الجَوابُ عَنْ حِصارِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) أهْلَ الطّائِفِ، واسْتِصْحابِهِ الحِصارَ إلى أنْ دَخَلَ الشَّهْرُ الحَرامُ، فَإنَّهُ مِن تَتِمَّةِ قِتالِ هَوازِنَ وأحْلافِها مِن ثَقِيفٍ، فَإنَّهم هُمُ الَّذِينَ ابْتَدَؤُوا القِتالَ، وجَمَعُوا الرِّجالَ، ودَعَوْا إلى الحَرْبِ والنِّزالِ، فَعِنْدَها قَصَدَهم رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) كَما تَقَدَّمَ، فَلَمّا تَحَصَّنُوا بِالطّائِفِ، ذَهَبَ إلَيْهِمْ لِيُنْزِلَهم مِن حُصُونِهِمْ، فَنالُوا مِنَ المُسْلِمِينَ، وقَتَلُوا جَماعَةً، واسْتَمَرَّ الحِصارُ بِالمَجانِيقِ وغَيْرِها قَرِيبًا مِن أرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا، وكانَ ابْتِداؤُهُ في شَهْرٍ حَلالٍ، ودَخَلَ الشَّهْرُ الحَرامُ، فاسْتَمَرَّ فِيهِ أيّامًا، ثُمَّ قَفَلَ عَنْهم، لِأنَّهُ يُغْتَفَرُ في الدَّوامِ ما لا يُغْتَفَرُ في الِابْتِداءِ، وهَذا أمْرٌ مُقَرَّرٌ، ولَهُ نَظائِرُ كَثِيرَةٌ.

فالمُحَرَّمُ هو ابْتِداءُ القِتالِ في الأشْهُرِ الحَرامِ، لا إتْمامُهُ، وبِهَذا يَحْصُلُ الجَمْعُ. ولِذا قالَ ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ: حَلَفَ بِاللَّهِ عَطاءُ بْنُ أبِي رَباحٍ: ما يَحِلُّ لِلنّاسِ أنْ يَغْزُوا في الحَرَمِ، ولا في الأشْهُرِ الحُرُمِ، وما نُسِخَتْ إلّا أنْ يُقاتِلُوا فِيها.

الثّامِنَةُ: قالَ في (" الإكْلِيلِ ") في قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿إنَّ عِدَّةَ الشُّهُورِ﴾ (سورة التوبة: ٣٦) الآيَةَ: إنَّ اللَّهَ وضَعَ هَذِهِ الأشْهُرَ وسَمّاها ورَتَّبَها عَلى ما هي عَلَيْهِ، وأنْزَلَ ذَلِكَ عَلى أنْبِيائِهِ، فَيُسْتَدَلُّ بِها لِمَن قالَ: إنَّ اللُّغاتِ تَوْقِيفِيَّةٌ (tawqifiyya: أي أنها من عند الله بالوحي لا باصطلاح البشر).

التّاسِعَةُ: في (" الإكْلِيلِ ") أيْضًا: اسْتَدَلَّ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وقاتِلُوا المُشْرِكِينَ كافَّةً﴾ (سورة التوبة: ٣٦) مَن قالَ إنَّ الجِهادَ في عَهْدِهِ (ﷺ) كانَ فَرْضَ عَيْنٍ (fard 'ayn: الواجب على كل مكلف بعينه).

العاشِرَةُ: قالَ ابْنُ إسْحاقَ: كانَ أوَّلَ مَن نَسَأ الشُّهُورَ عَلى العَرَبِ (nasa' al-shuhur: تأخير حرمة شهر إلى شهر آخر)، فَأحَلَّ مِنها ما حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ، وحَرَّمَ مِنها ما أحَلَّ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وجَلَّ (القَلَمَّسُ)، وهو حُذَيْفَةُ بْنُ عَبْدِ فُقَيْمِ بْنِ عَدِيِّ بْنِ عامِرِ بْنِ ثَعْلَبَةَ بْنِ الحارِثِ بْنِ مالِكِ بْنِ كِنانَةَ بْنِ خُزَيْمَةَ بْنِ مُدْرِكَةَ بْنِ إلْياسَ بْنِ مُضَرَ بْنِ نِزارِ بْنِ مَعَدِّ بْنِ عَدْنانَ، ثُمَّ قامَ بَعْدَهُ عَلى ذَلِكَ ابْنُهُ عَبّادٌ، ثُمَّ ابْنُهُ قَلَعٌ، ثُمَّ أُمَيَّةُ بْنُ قَلَعٍ، ثُمَّ ابْنُهُ عَوْفُ بْنُ أُمَيَّةَ، ثُمَّ ابْنُهُ أبُو ثُمامَةَ جُنادَةُ بْنُ (p-٣١٥٣) عَوْفٍ، وكانَ آخِرَهم، وعَلَيْهِ قامَ الإسْلامُ، فَكانَتِ العَرَبُ إذا فَرَغَتْ مِن حَجِّها، اجْتَمَعَتْ إلَيْهِ، فَقامَ فِيهِمْ خَطِيبًا فَحَرَّمَ رَجَبًا، وذا القِعْدَةِ، وذا الحِجَّةِ، ويُحِلُّ المُحَرَّمَ (عامًا)، ويَجْعَلُ مَكانَهُ (صَفَرَ)، ويُحَرِّمُهُ عامًا، لِيُواطِئَ عِدَّةَ ما حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ، فَيُحِلَّ ما حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ، يَعْنِي ويُحَرِّمَ ما أحَلَّ اللَّهُ. انْتَهى.

و(القَلَمَّسُ) بِقافٍ فَلامٍ مَفْتُوحَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ مِيمٍ مُشَدَّدَةٍ. قالَ في (" القامُوسِ وشَرْحِهِ "): هو رَجُلٌ كِنانِيٌّ مِن نَسَأةِ الشُّهُورِ عَلى مَعَدٍّ في الجاهِلِيَّةِ، كانَ يَقِفُ عِنْدَ جَمْرَةِ العَقَبَةِ ويَقُولُ: اللَّهُمَّ إنِّي ناسِئُ الشُّهُورِ، وواضِعُها مَواضِعَها، ولا أُعابُ ولا أُحابُ. اللَّهُمَّ إنِّي قَدْ أحْلَلْتُ أحَدَ الصَّفَرَيْنِ، وحَرَّمْتُ صَفَرَ المُؤَخَّرَ، وكَذا في الرَّجَبَيْنِ (يَعْنِي رَجَبًا وشَعْبانَ)، ثُمَّ يَقُولُ: انْفِرُوا عَلى اسْمِ اللَّهِ تَعالى. قالَ شاعِرُهم:

وفِينا ناسِئُ الشَّهْرِ القَلَمَّسُ

وقالَ عُمَيْرُ بْنُ قَيْسٍ المَعْرُوفُ بِجَذْلِ الطِّعانِ:

لَقَدْ عَلِمَتْ مَعَدٌّ أنَّ قَوْمِي * كِرامُ النّاسِ أنَّ لَهم كِراما
أَلَسْنا النّاسِئِينَ عَلى مَعَدٍّ * شُهُورَ الحِلِّ نَجْعَلُها حَراما
فَأيُّ النّاسِ فاتُونا بِوِتْرٍ * وأيُّ النّاسِ لَمْ نُعْلِكْ لِجاما

ورُوِيَ أنَّ أوَّلَ مَن سَنَّ النَّسِيءَ عَمْرُو بْنُ لُحَيٍّ، والَّذِي صَحَّ مِن حَدِيثِ أبِي هُرَيْرَةَ (p-٣١٥٤) وعائِشَةَ: «أنَّ عَمْرَو بْنَ لُحَيٍّ أوَّلُ مَن سَيَّبَ السَّوائِبَ، وقالَ فِيهِ النَّبِيُّ (ﷺ): "رَأيْتُ عَمْرَو بْنَ لُحَيٍّ يَجُرُّ قُصْبَهُ في النّارِ"».

ثُمَّ حَرَّضَ تَعالى المُؤْمِنِينَ عَلى قِتالِ الكَفَرَةِ، إثْرَ بَيانِ طَرَفٍ مِن قَبائِحِهِمُ المُوجِبَةِ لِذَلِكَ، وأشارَ إلى تَوَجُّهِ العِتابِ والمَلامَةِ إلى المُتَخَلِّفِينَ عَنْهُ، بِقَوْلِهِ سُبْحانَهُ:

**The discussion on the interpretation of His, exalted is He, saying:**

[ 38 ] ﴿O you who have believed, what is [wrong] with you that when you are told, "Go forth in the way of Allah," you adhere heavily to the earth? Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter? But the enjoyment of worldly life, compared to the Hereafter, is little.﴾

His saying, ﴿to the earth﴾, is connected to ﴿adhere heavily﴾ by way of *taḍmīn* (a verb being given the sense of another verb, here implying inclination and settling), meaning: you adhered heavily, inclining towards this world and its perishable desires for a little while, and you disliked the hardships of the campaign, which lead to lasting comfort. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and he inclined towards the earth and followed his desire﴾ [al-A'raf: 176].

Or it means: inclining to remain in your land and your homes. This was at the Battle of Tabuk, in the ninth year [of the Hijra] (the text says the tenth year) after their return from al-Ta'if. They were called to fight the Romans in a time of hardship, drought and scorching heat, when the fruits of Madinah had ripened and its shade was pleasant, along with the great distance and the large number of the enemy. So it was difficult for them.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Are you satisfied with the life of this world﴾, meaning: the base and perishable [life]; ﴿rather than the Hereafter﴾, meaning: in exchange for the Hereafter and its everlasting bliss. ﴿But the enjoyment of worldly life﴾: the noun is stated explicitly in place of a pronoun, for the sake of emphasis; meaning, the enjoyment of its pleasures ﴿compared to the Hereafter﴾, meaning: in comparison with the Hereafter, when it is measured against it. This *fī* (in) is called *fī al-qiyāsiyya* (the "in" of measurement), because the thing being measured is placed beside that by which it is measured. ﴿is little﴾, meaning: insignificant, not given any regard.

Imam Ahmad and Muslim narrated from al-Mustawrid, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The world, compared to the Hereafter, is nothing but like one of you putting this finger of his into the sea; let him see with what it returns," and he pointed with the index finger.

Then, exalted is He, threatened those who did not go forth to the campaign, with His saying, glory be to Him:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[39] ﴿Unless you go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment and replace you with another people, and you will not harm Him at all. And Allah is over all things competent.﴾

﴿Unless you go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment and replace you with another people other than you﴾, that is, for the support of His Prophet and the establishment of His religion. ﴿And you will not harm Him at all﴾, because He is the Free of need from the worlds; that is, rather, you harm only yourselves. It has also been said: the pronoun refers to the Messenger ﷺ, meaning, "and you will not harm him," because Allah has promised him victory, and His promise is certainly going to be fulfilled.

﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾, that is, to punish and to replace, and to support His religion through others besides them. In this threat against those who stay behind from the raid there is a dreadful intimidation whose extent cannot be measured.

Admonition:

Some of the scholars said: the fruit of the verse is the obligation to respond to the Messenger ﷺ when he calls to jihad; likewise the same applies to the call of the leaders (imams). Like jihad, the call to all other obligatory duties also applies, and in this there is emphasis from several aspects:

First: what he mentioned of reproach.

(p-3156) Second: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You clung heavily to the earth﴾ [al-Tawbah: 38], and that the inclination toward benefits, ease, and pleasures does not constitute a concession in this matter.

Third: in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Are you pleased with the life of this world?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 38], so this is a rebuke.

Fourth: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then what is the enjoyment...﴾ [al-Tawbah: 38], the verse. This is a belittling of their opinion.

Fifth: the threat that He followed with His saying: ﴿Unless you go forth, He will punish you﴾.

Sixth: what he exaggerated in with His saying: ﴿a painful punishment﴾.

Seventh: His saying: ﴿and replace﴾, the verse.

Eighth: His saying: ﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾, for in it is a threat.

And His saying, exalted is He:

The discussion of the words of God Most High:

[40] ﴿If you do not support him, then Allah has already supported him when those who disbelieved expelled him, the second of two. When they were both in the cave, when he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us." So Allah sent down His tranquility upon him and supported him with soldiers you did not see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest; and the word of Allah is the highest. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.﴾

﴿If you do not support him﴾ i.e., by going out with him to Tabuk. ﴿then Allah has already supported him when those who disbelieved expelled him﴾

That is, the disbelievers of Makkah, when they plotted against him, became the cause of his departure. He went out, and with him was Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him. ﴿The second of two﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) referring to his pronoun ﷺ, i.e., one of two. ﴿When they were both in the cave﴾ is a substitution (badal) for ﴿when he expelled him﴾, a partial substitution (badal al-ba'd), since the intended meaning is an extended period of time.

The cave (al-ghar) is a hollow at the top of Thawr, a mountain on the right side of Makkah at a distance of one hour's journey. They remained in it for three days, so that the pursuers who had gone out following their tracks would return, and then they would proceed to Madinah. ﴿When he said﴾ is a second substitution, i.e., (p-3157) the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ﴿to his companion﴾, i.e., Abu Bakr: ﴿Do not grieve.﴾ This was because Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, feared that the polytheists would learn of their location, so harm would reach the Messenger ﷺ, and he began to be distressed by this. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾, i.e., with support and protection.

Imam Ahmad and the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated from Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I looked at the feet of the polytheists while we were in the cave, and they were over our heads. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah! If one of them were to look at his feet, he would see us beneath his feet!' He said: 'O Abu Bakr! What do you think of two whose third is Allah?'"

﴿So Allah sent down His tranquility﴾, i.e., His security in which hearts find rest, ﴿upon him﴾, i.e., upon the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿and supported him with soldiers you did not see﴾, meaning the angels, whom He sent down to guard him in the cave, or to help him against the enemy on the day of Badr, the Confederates, and Hunayn. Thus the clause is coordinated with His saying: ﴿Allah supported him.﴾ Abu al-Su'ud favoured the second interpretation, arguing that the first is contradicted by the description of them as unseen by those addressed.

I say: there is no contradiction, because this description is a necessary attribute of the supply of unseen strength in every situation, while the second view creates a disjointed style due to the distance between the two coordinated elements. Understand this. And Allah knows best.

﴿And made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest﴾, i.e., the defeated and subdued. The "word" is shirk, or the call to disbelief. It is a metaphor for their creed, which it is their nature to speak, on the basis that it is shirk; or it means speech in general, on the basis that it is the call to disbelief. ﴿And the word of Allah is the highest﴾, meaning monotheism, or the call of Islam as mentioned earlier, i.e., that which remains high until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And the word of Allah﴾ with the nominative (raf') as the subject (mubtada'), and ﴿is the highest﴾ is the predicate (khabar). Or "hiya" (it) may be a separator (fasl).

It has been read in the accusative, i.e., "and made the word of Allah," but the first reading is more eloquent and emphatic, because the nominal sentence indicates permanence and stability, and "making" does not apply to it, since in itself it is high, its state never changes and its condition never alters. The attribution of "the word" to "Allah" elevates its station and honours its status. ﴿And Allah is Exalted in Might﴾, i.e., dominant over what He wills; ﴿Wise﴾ in His judgement and His management.

Note:

Some commentators of the Zaydiyya said: the high station of Abu Bakr is established from this verse in several ways. Among them: the words of God Most High ﴿when he said to his companion, "Do not grieve"﴾ and His saying ﴿indeed Allah is with us﴾ and His saying ﴿so Allah sent down His tranquility upon him﴾. It has been said: upon Abu Bakr. This is from Abu 'Ali and al-Asamm; Abu 'Ali said: because he was the one who feared and needed security. It has also been said: upon the Messenger, from al-Zajjaj and Abu Muslim.

Jar Allah (al-Zamakhshari) said: They have said: whoever denies the companionship of Abu Bakr has disbelieved, because he has rejected the Book of Allah Most High. End.

And al-Suyuti said in "al-Iklil": Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "I, by Allah, am his companion." Hence the Malikis said: whoever denies the companionship of Abu Bakr disbelieves and is to be killed, unlike other Companions, due to the explicit text of the Qur'an concerning his companionship. End.

From Ibn 'Umar: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abu Bakr: 'You are my companion at the Basin (al-Hawd), and my companion in the cave.'" Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who said: a hasan gharib hadith.

Al-Fakhr al-Razi has presented twelve aspects from this verse concerning the virtue of al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, and he elaborated and did well.

When Allah Most High threatened those who do not go forth with the Messenger to Tabuk, and set forth for them examples containing the greatest warning, He followed this with this decisive command, so He, glorified be He, said:

[p. 3159]

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[41] ﴿Go forth, whether light or heavy, and strive with your wealth and your lives in the way of God. That is better for you, if you only knew.﴾

﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ are two circumstantial clauses (ḥāl) referring to the pronoun of the addressees. The meaning is: in whatever state you are, light (for going forth) because of your eagerness for it, or heavy (reluctant) because of its hardship for you. Or "light" means having few dependents and encumbrances, and "heavy" means having many. Or "light" means lightly armed and "heavy" means heavily armed. Or "light" means riding and "heavy" means on foot. Or "light" means young and "heavy" means old. Or "light" means lean and "heavy" means fat. The noble wording covers all of this, and what is meant is the state of ease in going forth and the state of its difficulty.

It has been related from a group of the Companions that they never lagged behind from any military expedition (ghazwa), and they cited this verse as evidence.

When the expeditions were sent to al-Shām (Syria), Abū Ṭalḥa, may God be pleased with him, was reciting Sūrat Barā'a until he reached this verse. He said: "I see that our Lord has called us to go forth, old and young. Prepare me, my sons!" His sons said: "May God have mercy on you. You fought alongside the Messenger of God ﷺ until he died, alongside Abū Bakr until he died, and alongside ʿUmar until he died. So we will fight on your behalf." He said: "No excuse of anyone has been accepted." Then he set out for al-Shām and fought until he was killed.

Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī, may God be pleased with him, used to recite this verse and say: "I find myself only light or heavy." He did not lag behind from any expedition of the Muslims except for one year.

Abū Rāshid al-Ḥarrānī said: "I came upon al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad, the horseman of the Messenger of God ﷺ, sitting on a chest from the chests of the money-changers in Ḥimṣ, having set out from it intending the raid. I said to him: 'God has already excused you.' He said: 'The Sūrat of the expeditions has come upon us: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾.'"

On the authority of Ḥayyān ibn Zayd, who said: "We went forth with Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr, who was governor of Ḥimṣ. I saw an old man, decrepit, whose eyebrows had fallen over his eyes, from the people of Damascus, on his mount among those who were raiding. I approached him and said: 'O uncle, God has already excused you.' He raised his eyebrows and said: 'O nephew! God has called us to go forth, light and heavy. Indeed, whomever God loves, He tests; then God restores him and keeps him alive. God only tests from among His servants those who give thanks, endure patiently, and remember Him, and worship none but God, Mighty and Majestic.'" Ibn Jarīr (al-Ṭabarī) narrated all of this.

May God have mercy on those pure souls, and greet them as brave warriors, who sold their lives seeking the pleasure of their Lord and the exaltation of His Word, and who honoured themselves by refusing to be deceived by the adornments of this lowly life.

Then He, exalted is He, encouraged spending in His way and giving up one's lives seeking His pleasure and the pleasure of His Messenger, saying: ﴿and strive with your wealth and your lives in the way of God. That is better for you, if you only knew.﴾ The demonstrative (dhālika) referring to the going forth and the striving carries a sense of distance, to signal the elevation of its rank in nobility. What is meant by its being "better" is that it is good in itself, or that it is better than ease and enjoying wealth.

**Note (tanbīh):**

Al-Ḥākim said: Striving with wealth takes several forms. Among them is spending on oneself during the march in jihad; among them is spending on the equipment by which one is aided in jihad; and among them is spending on one who acts on one's behalf or goes out with one.

Some of the exegetes of the Zaydiyya (a Shiʿi school) said: al-Mu'ayyad billāh mentioned that whoever has an excess of wealth is obliged to hand it over to the Imam (ruler), if need calls for it.

And al-Rāḍī billāh mentioned the obligation of giving whatever wealth the need calls for in jihad, whether little or much, and that this becomes specifically required when the Imam designates it.

As for the way of ḥisba (the public duty of enforcing what serves the common good), al-Rāḍī billāh said: it is obligatory if a breach occurs that only wealth can fill. This includes compelling the provision of hospitality and the billeting of soldiers in houses. Al-Rāḍī billāh also said: the Imam may compel the subjects to whatever he sees as beneficial.

(p. 3160 / 3161) It is also related from al-Mu'ayyad billāh that the Imam may quarter his army in the homes of the subjects if the commanding of good and forbidding of evil cannot be achieved except by the troops, and they need that. Just as it is permissible to enter a usurped house in order to remove an evil.

Likewise Abū Muḍar mentioned that he (the army) may lodge in what exceeds the needs of the people of the houses. As for a soldier from his army who lodges in a house by oppression or corruption, if that is known, then the Imam's demand to repel the evil is weighed against this evil committed by the troops, to see which of the two is graver. End of quote.

Then, exalted is He, turned the address away from those who stayed behind and directed it to the Messenger of God ﷺ, enumerating the lapses that proceeded from them in word and deed, showing the baseness of their aspirations in this matter. So He, glorified is He, said:

The Discourse on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[42] ﴿Had it been a near gain and an easy journey, they would have followed you, but the distance seemed long to them. They will swear by God, "Had we been able, we would have gone out with you." They destroy themselves, and God knows that they are liars.﴾

﴿Had it been﴾ means: what you call them to. ﴿A near gain﴾ means: a benefit easy to obtain. ﴿And an easy journey﴾ means: a moderate one. ﴿They would have followed you﴾ means: not for your sake, but to suit their desires. ﴿But the distance seemed long to them﴾ is read with a dammah on the shin (ash-shuqqah), and it is also read with a kasrah (a recognised variant reading). It means the destination to which they were summoned. The destination that a traveller aims for is called by this name because of the hardship (mashaqqah) that befalls him in reaching it.

It is also read as (ba'idat) with a kasrah on the ayn. Al-Shihab said: "Ba'ida yab'adu is like 'alima ya'lamu, a dialect form of it, but it is mostly restricted to distance in the sense of death." And (la tab'ud), is used in calamities to express grief and sorrow, as in his saying:

"May God not let our brothers who have departed be far away; the vicissitudes of time and eternity have consumed them."

﴿They will swear﴾ means: these who stayed behind from the expedition of Tabuk. ﴿By God﴾ is connected to ﴿they will swear﴾, or it is part of their own speech.

The phrase "saying" is implied in both cases. That is, they will swear when you return from the expedition of Tabuk, offering the excuse of incapacity, saying by God: ﴿Had we been able, we would have gone out with you﴾, that is, to that expedition.

Then God, Exalted, made clear that this false claim and this oath would not benefit them, in His saying: ﴿They destroy themselves﴾, that is, by this oath, this disobedience and this claim of incapacity. ﴿And God knows that they are liars﴾, because they were able to go out with the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, Exalted is He:

[43] ﴿May Allah pardon you. Why did you give them permission (to stay behind) until those who were truthful became clear to you and you knew the liars?﴾

That is: for these hypocrites, in staying behind, when they offered their excuses. ﴿Until those who were truthful became clear to you and you knew the liars﴾ means: would that you had left them when they asked your permission and had not granted any of them permission to remain behind, so that you would know which of them were truthful in displaying obedience to you and which were liars, for they had been insistent on remaining behind from the expedition.

Therefore Allah, Exalted is He, informed that no one who believes in Allah and His Messenger asks His permission to remain behind from the expedition, by His saying, Glorified is He:

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[44] ﴿Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask your permission to strive with their wealth and their lives. And Allah is Knowing of the God-conscious.﴾
