The discussion of the words of His exalted saying:

[115] ﴿And Allah would never misguide a people after He had guided them until He makes clear to them what they should fear.﴾ Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.

﴿And Allah would never misguide a people after He had guided them until He makes clear to them what they should fear⁠﴾ This is a continuation of what preceded regarding the emphatic disassociation from the polytheists, the disavowal of them, and abandoning seeking forgiveness for them. That is because the word had become binding upon them, since the proof was established against them by the Messenger's conveying to them what they should fear, and his guidance of them to the right path, yet they went astray from it. So Allah misguided them, and they deserved His punishment.

His exalted saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things⁠﴾ is a justification for what preceded; that is, He, exalted is He, is Knowing of all things, among which is their need for an explanation of the ugliness of what the intellect cannot independently know. So He made that clear to them, as He has done here.

And His exalted saying:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[116] ﴿Indeed, to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death. And you have not, other than Allah, any ally or any helper.﴾

﴿Indeed, to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death. And you have not, other than Allah, any ally or any helper.﴾ This reinforces what preceded regarding disavowal of them, and it guides the believers to rely upon their Lord and not to fear those people, for when He is their helper, their scheming cannot harm them. It also serves as a reminder of the necessity of complying with His command, submitting to His judgment, and turning to Him alone, since no one can obtain guardianship or support except from Him, exalted is He.

A caution:

Many of the exegetes paused at this verse, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah would never misguide a people﴾ [al-Tawbah: 115] and what follows, according to what was narrated concerning the occasion of its revelation in the previous verse, regarding a plea for forgiveness that the believers made for the polytheists. They linked this verse with that one, on the basis of the aforementioned narration, and applied it to the believers, saying: ﴿And Allah would never misguide a people﴾ [al-Tawbah: 115], meaning: He would not pass judgment upon them as being astray for their asking forgiveness for the polytheists after He had guided them through prophethood and faith, until He sends forth to them a prohibition against it, and then they abandon it. But if He has not made it clear, then there is no misguidance, to the end of what they said. . . .

How far removed from the truth is the tafsir and interpretation of al-Razi, which he mentioned as one possibility. I corroborate it with what we have relied upon, and that is the truth.

The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 9, Verse 117:

(p-3285) The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying:

[117] ﴿Certainly Allah has turned in forgiveness toward the Prophet and the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship, after the hearts of a faction of them had nearly deviated. Then He turned to them in forgiveness. Indeed, He is Kind and Merciful to them.﴾

﴿Certainly Allah has turned in forgiveness toward the Prophet and the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship, after the hearts of a faction of them had nearly deviated. Then He turned to them in forgiveness. Indeed, He is Kind and Merciful to them.﴾

Know that when Allah, the Exalted, had explained earlier the ranks of people during the days of the Battle of Tabuk, the believers and the hypocrites among them, those who spent for it willingly or unwillingly, those who encouraged others to it or discouraged them from it, and those who stayed behind out of hypocrisy or laziness, and had informed of what befell each of them of promise and threat, and had distinguished the truthful from others, He concluded with a group of them who had stayed behind out of inclination to ease, while they were truthful in their faith. Then they regretted, repented and turned back in contrition, and Allah knew the sincerity of their repentance, so He accepted it. Then He revealed their repentance in this verse, and He introduced it with His turning in forgiveness toward His Messenger and the senior members of his Companions, to console their hearts and to honour their station by linking them with those about whom He is definitively pleased, and to urge the believers toward repentance. Every believer, indeed, is in need of repentance and seeking forgiveness, even the Prophet, the Emigrants and the Helpers, each according to his own measure. It also demonstrates the excellence and the worth of repentance in the sight of Allah, and that the attribute of those who repent much and turn back often is the attribute of the prophets, just as He described them as righteous, in order to show the virtue of righteousness. The description serves to praise, just as it may serve to praise the one described; the praise of the attribute is the same as the praise of the one who bears it. This is among the subtleties of eloquence, and it is as Hassan, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

؎ما إنْ مَدَحْتُ مُحَمَّدًا بِمَقالَتِي لَكِنْ مَدَحْتُ مَقالَتِي بِمُحَمَّدِ

[Verse:] I have not praised Muhammad with my speech; rather, I have praised my speech through Muhammad.

In the verse there is a clear demonstration of the excellence of the Emigrants and the Helpers.

(p-3286) Al-Hakim said: It also indicates the excellence of Uthman, because he equipped the army of hardship with wealth that no one else reached the level of. Allah, the Exalted, has united the mention of His Prophet with the mention of them, and described them as following him, so it is obligatory to affirm their allegiance with certainty.

As for His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿in the hour of hardship﴾, it means in its time. The word "sa'a" (hour) is used to mean unrestricted time, just as "ghadah" (morning), "ashiyyah" (evening) and "yawm" (day) are used. The hardship (ʿusrah) was their condition in the Battle of Tabuk: they were in hardship regarding mounts, with ten men taking turns on a single camel; and in hardship regarding provisions, to the point that two men would split a date between them, and a group would pass a date among themselves, one sucking it and drinking water over it, then the next sucking it and drinking over it. And they were in hardship because of the intensity of the blazing heat and the drought, and in hardship regarding water, to the point that thirst reached one of them so that he slaughtered his camel, squeezed out its stomach contents, drank them, and put what remained on his liver.

Al-Qali related in his "Amali" that the Arabs, when they wished to traverse deserts in which there was no water, would give their camels their fill of water and then cut their muzzles or pierce their nostrils so that they could not graze; then when they needed water they would slit open their paunches and drink the water within them, which is frequently mentioned in poetry. Thus it is in (al-'Inayah).

Al-Razi transmitted from Abu Muslim that the intended meaning of "the hour of hardship" may be all the difficult circumstances and times faced by the Messenger and the believers, so that it includes the Battle of the Trench and others.

He, the Exalted, has mentioned some of them in His Book, such as His, the Glorified's, saying: ﴿And when the eyes swerved and the hearts reached the throats﴾ [al-Ahzab: 10], and His saying: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission, until when you lost courage﴾ [Al 'Imran: 152]. The purpose of this is to describe the Emigrants and the Helpers as having followed the Messenger ﷺ in the severe times and the difficult circumstances, and this conveys the utmost of praise and magnification. End.

(p-3287) I say: This interpretation, although the noble wording can bear it, is far from it by the context and the immediate context of the verse, both of which are confined to the Battle of Tabuk; hardship in departure and following him, peace be upon him, did not occur in any other campaign, rather he sometimes occurred in the battle lines of combat.

The scholars of narration and biography have agreed on calling it (the Battle of Hardship), and those who went out in it (the Army of Hardship).

As for His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿after the hearts of a faction of them had nearly deviated﴾, it means from the truth, or from steadfastness in following, because of the hardship and difficulty that befell them on their journey.

The repetition of the turning in forgiveness toward them in His saying: ﴿Then He turned to them in forgiveness﴾ is a clear emphasis and concern for its matter. This is if the pronoun refers back to those whose repentance was previously mentioned; if the pronoun refers to the second faction, then there is no repetition.

Some of them said: The mention of repentance first, before the mention of the sin, is out of His bounty and to comfort their hearts. Then He mentioned the sin after that, and followed it with the mention of repentance once more, to magnify their standing and so that they would know that He, the Exalted, had accepted their repentance and pardoned them. Then He followed it with His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is Kind and Merciful to them﴾ as an affirmation of that.

And His, the Exalted's, saying:

The commentary on His saying, exalted is He:

[118] ﴿And [He also forgave] the three who were left behind, until when the earth became constricted for them despite its vastness, and their souls became constricted for them, and they thought that there was no refuge from God except in Him. Then He turned to them so that they might repent. Indeed, God is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

﴿And [He also forgave] the three who were left behind﴾ means they were left and delayed from having their repentance accepted immediately, just as the repentance of those who stayed behind, mentioned earlier, had been accepted. The three were Ka'b ibn Malik, Murarah ibn al-Rabi', and Hilal ibn Umayyah, and all of them were from the Ansar (the Helpers). The Prophet (ﷺ) did not accept their repentance until the Qur'an was revealed concerning their repentance.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿until when the earth became constricted for them despite its vastness﴾ means: despite its breadth. This is like bewilderment in their affair, as if they could find no place in it in which to settle, out of restlessness and anguish at what they were in. Since the Prophet (ﷺ) had forbidden people from sitting with them and speaking with them, they could not go to anyone. Regarding ﴿إذا﴾ (idha), it may be conditional (shartiyyah) with its response (jawab) omitted, or it may be temporal (zarfiyyah), indicating the endpoint (ghayah) of what precedes it.

﴿And their souls became constricted for them﴾ means their hearts, from the extreme of loneliness, estrangement, and grief, such that no comfort or joy could contain them. This was because they kept to their houses and abandoned [the community] for about fifty nights. In this there is an ascent (taraqqi) from the constriction of the earth to the constriction within their souls, and it is of the utmost eloquence (balaghah).

﴿And they thought﴾ means they knew ﴿that there was no refuge from God﴾, meaning no escape from the anger of God, ﴿except in Him﴾, meaning except in seeking His forgiveness. ﴿Then He turned to them so that they might repent﴾ means so that they would remain steadfast in their repentance and persist in it, or so that they would be counted among those who repent. Or the meaning is: [He turned to them] before their repentance, so that they would repent in the future whenever a lapse proceeded from them, and would not despair of His generosity. ﴿Indeed, God is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 9, verse 119 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:
[119] ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful.﴾ That is: in their faith and in their pledge to Allah and His Messenger to obey, from His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they pledged to Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 23]. Or it refers to the three (who were forgiven), meaning: be like them in their truthfulness and the sincerity of their intention.

Remarks:

The first: Imam Ahmad, al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated the hadith of Ka'b and his two companions in full detail, which clarifies this verse.

al-Zuhri said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik informed me, from his father, who was the guide of Ka'b from among his sons after he went blind, that he said: "I heard Ka'b narrate his account when he stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the expedition of Tabuk."

[p. 3289] Ka'b said: "I never stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in any expedition he undertook, except the expedition of Tabuk. However, I had stayed behind from the expedition of Badr, and no one who stayed behind from it was rebuked. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) only went out seeking the caravan of Quraysh, until Allah brought them together with their enemy without prior appointment.

And I witnessed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the night of 'Aqabah, when we pledged together to Islam, and I would not like to exchange it for the witnessing of Badr, though Badr is more mentioned among the people and more famous.

As for my account when I stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the expedition of Tabuk: I was never stronger or more well-off than I was when I stayed behind from him in that expedition. By Allah, I had never before owned two riding camels, but I owned both of them in that expedition.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rarely intended an expedition he would undertake without giving the impression of going elsewhere, until that expedition came. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) undertook it in intense heat, facing a long journey, deserts, and a numerous enemy. He therefore made clear to the Muslims their matter, so that they might prepare themselves for the readiness of their enemy, and he informed them of the direction he intended. The Muslims with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were many and had no book to register them, meaning the register (diwan)."

Ka'b said: "Few men wished to absent themselves but thought it would remain hidden from them, so long as no revelation came down about it from Allah, mighty and majestic."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out on that expedition when the fruits and shade had ripened, and I was inclined towards them, meaning: I was attracted to them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prepared for it, and the believers with him. I began to go out in the morning to prepare with them, then I would return without having done anything for my equipment. I would say to myself: 'I am capable of that whenever I wish.' This continued with me until the people became serious, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out in the morning, with the Muslims with him, while I had done nothing for my equipment. I said: 'I will prepare a day or two after him, then I will catch up with him.' So I went out later to prepare, then returned having done nothing. This continued with me until they hastened and the expedition had gone ahead. I intended to set out and catch up with them, and I wish I had done so, but that was not decreed for me.

So whenever I went out among the people after the departure of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), it grieved me that I saw none but a man openly accused of hypocrisy, or a man whom Allah, mighty and majestic, had excused. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not mention me until he reached Tabuk. Then he said while sitting among the people at Tabuk: 'What has Ka'b ibn Malik done?' A man from the Banu Salamah said: 'O Messenger of Allah, his two cloaks and his looking at his own sides have held him back!' Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: 'How evil was what you said! By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we know nothing of him but good!' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was silent.

[p. 3290] Ka'b ibn Malik said: "When it reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had turned back from Tabuk on his return, my distress was aroused, and I began to think of lies, saying: 'By what shall I escape his displeasure tomorrow?' And I sought help in that from every wise person among my family.

When it was said that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was about to arrive, falsehood departed from me, and I knew that I would never escape from it by anything at all. So I resolved to be truthful with him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in the morning — and when he returned from a journey he would begin with the mosque, pray two rak'ahs, then sit for the people. When he did that, those who had stayed behind came to him, began to make excuses to him and swear oaths to him. They were some eighty men. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted their outward profession, asked forgiveness for them, and left their inner states to Allah, exalted is He. Until I came, and when I greeted him, he smiled the smile of one who is angry. Then he said to me: 'Come here!' So I came walking until I sat before him. He said to me: 'What held you back? Had you not bought a mount?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah! If I were sitting before anyone other than you among the people of this world, I would have considered escaping his displeasure with an excuse. I have been given skill in argument, but by Allah, I know that if I told you today a lie by which you would be pleased with me, Allah would soon make you displeased with me. And if I tell you the truth, by which you will find fault with me, I hope for its good outcome from Allah, mighty and majestic. By Allah, I had no excuse. By Allah, I was never more able or more well-off than when I stayed behind from you.'"

He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'As for this one, he has spoken the truth. Stand up until Allah decides concerning you!' So I stood up, and men from the Banu Salamah rose to me and followed me. They said to me: 'By Allah, we did not know you to have committed a sin before this. You were unable to make an excuse to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) like the excuses made by those who stayed behind. The Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) seeking forgiveness for you would have been sufficient for your sin.'"

He said: "By Allah, they did not stop until I wanted to return and call myself a liar."

He said: "Then I said to them: 'Did anyone else meet this with me?' They said: 'Yes, two men met it with you, and they said what you said, and they were told what you were told.' I said: 'Who are they?' They said: 'Murarah ibn al-Rabi' al-'Amiri and Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqifi.' They mentioned to me two righteous men who had witnessed Badr, in whom there is an example for me."

[p. 3291] He said: "So I went on when they mentioned them to me."

He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade us from speaking, we three, from among those who had stayed behind. So the people avoided us and changed towards us, until the earth seemed strange to me within myself, not the earth I had known. We remained in that state for fifty nights.

As for my two companions, they grew humble and sat in their houses weeping. As for me, I was the strongest and most steadfast of the people. I would attend the prayer with the Muslims and walk through the markets, but no one spoke to me. I would come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was in his assembly after the prayer, and I would greet him, and say to myself: 'Did he move his lips to return the greeting to me or not?' Then I would pray near him and steal glances at him. When I turned to my prayer, he would look at me, and when I turned towards him, he would turn away from me.

When this lasted long for me because of the avoidance of the Muslims, I walked until I climbed over the wall of Abu Qatadah, who was my cousin and the most beloved of people to me. I greeted him, and by Allah, he did not return my greeting. I said to him: 'O Abu Qatadah! I adjure you by Allah, do you know that I love Allah and His Messenger?' He was silent.

He said: 'I returned to him and adjured him, and he was silent. I returned to him and adjured him, and he was silent. Then he said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."' He said: 'My eyes overflowed, and I turned away until I climbed over the wall.

While I was walking in the market of Madinah, behold, a Nabataean from the Nabataeans of Syria, one of those who came with food to sell in Madinah, was saying: "Who will direct me to Ka'b ibn Malik?" The people began pointing to me, until he came and handed me a letter from the king of Ghassan. I was a writer, so in it was:

"To proceed: We have received word that your companion has treated you harshly. Allah has not made you a place of humiliation or of neglect. So come to us, and we will console you."

He said: "When I read it, I said: 'This too is part of the trial!'"

He said: "So I took it to the oven and set it alight with it, until forty nights of the fifty had passed. Behold, a messenger of the messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to me, saying: [p. 3292] 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commands you to separate from your wife.' He said: 'I said: "Shall I divorce her, or what shall I do?" He said: "No, separate from her and do not approach her."'

He said: 'He sent to my two companions with the same. He said: I said to my wife: "Go to your people and remain with them until Allah decides concerning this matter as He wills!"' He said: 'The wife of Hilal ibn Umayyah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah! Hilal is a weak old man with no servant. Would you dislike it if I served him?" He said: "No, but let him not approach you!" She said: "By Allah, he has no inclination toward anything, and by Allah, he has not ceased weeping since the matter that befell him until this day."'

He said: 'Some of my family said to me: "If only you had asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permission regarding your wife, for he permitted the wife of Hilal to serve him." He said: "I said: 'By Allah, I will not ask him permission regarding her, and I do not know what he would say about her if I asked him, for I am a young man."'

He said: 'We remained ten more nights, so the fifty nights were completed for us from the time he forbade speaking with us.'

He said: 'Then I prayed the dawn prayer on the fiftieth morning on the roof of one of our houses. While I was sitting in the state which Allah, exalted is He, mentioned concerning us, my soul had become constricted within me, and the earth had become constricted for me despite its vastness, I heard a crier who had climbed onto Mount Sal', calling with his loudest voice: "Rejoice, O Ka'b ibn Malik!" He said: "I fell down prostrating, and I knew that relief had come from Allah, mighty and majestic, with the acceptance of our repentance. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) announced the acceptance of Allah's repentance upon us when he prayed the dawn prayer. The people went to give us glad tidings, and bearers of good news went to my two companions. A man rode to me on a horse, and a runner from the Aslam tribe ran and climbed the mountain, and the voice was faster than the horse. When the one whose voice I had heard, giving me glad tidings, came to me, I took off my two garments and gave them to him in return for his good news. By Allah, I did not own any other garments that day, so I borrowed two garments and wore them, and I set out intending the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The people met me in groups, congratulating me on the repentance of Allah, saying: 'May the acceptance of Allah's repentance be a blessing for you!' Until I entered the mosque, and behold, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting in the mosque with the people around him. Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah rose to me, hurrying, until he shook my hand and congratulated me. By Allah, no man among the Muhajirun rose to me other than him."'

[p. 3293] He said: "Ka'b would never forget that for Talhah."

Ka'b said: "When I greeted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said, while his face was shining with joy: 'Rejoice in the best day that has passed over you since your mother bore you!' I said: 'Is it from you, O Messenger of Allah, or from Allah?' He said: 'No, rather it is from Allah.' He said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was pleased, his face would light up, until it was like a piece of the moon, so that this could be recognised from him. When I sat before him, I said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Part of my repentance is that I should withdraw from my wealth as a charity to Allah and His Messenger.' He said: 'Keep some of your wealth for yourself, for it is better for you.' I said: 'Then I will keep my share that is at Khaybar.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Allah only saved me through truthfulness, and part of my repentance is that I will speak only the truth as long as I live.' He said: 'By Allah, I know of no one among the Muslims whom Allah has tested in truthfulness in speech, since I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), better than the way Allah, exalted is He, has tested me. By Allah, I have not deliberately told a lie since I said that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until this day of mine, and I hope that Allah, mighty and majestic, will protect me in what remains.'"

He said: "Allah then sent down: ﴿Allah has certainly turned in forgiveness to the Prophet﴾ [al-Tawbah: 117], to the end of the verses."

Kaʿb said: "By Allah, after Allah guided me to Islam, no blessing ever bestowed upon me was greater in my soul than my truthfulness to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on that day, that I did not lie to him and so perish as those who lied perished. For Allah, the Exalted, said of those who lied, when the revelation was sent down, the worst that He said of anyone: ﴿They will swear to you by Allah when you return to them, that you may leave them alone. So leave them alone. Indeed, they are impure, and their refuge is Hell as recompense for what they used to earn.﴾ [At-Tawbah: 95] ﴿They swear to you that you may be pleased with them. But if you are pleased with them, indeed Allah is not pleased with a defiantly disobedient people.﴾ [At-Tawbah: 96]"

He said: "We, the three who were left behind, were [in a matter] other than the matter of those whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ accepted from when they were left behind. He accepted their pledges of allegiance, asked forgiveness for them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ deferred our matter until Allah decided concerning it. It is for this that He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And [He also forgave] the three who were left behind﴾ [At-Tawbah: 118]. What is meant is not that we were left behind from the expedition; rather, it is his leaving us behind and his deferring our matter, in contrast to those who swore to him and made excuses to him, and he accepted from them."

In another narration: "The Prophet ﷺ forbade people from speaking to me and to my two companions, and he did not forbid anyone else from among those who stayed behind besides us. So the people shunned our speech. I remained in that state until the matter grew long upon me. Nothing was more pressing to me than to die, lest the Prophet ﷺ not pray over me, or the Messenger of Allah ﷺ die while I remained in that station, no one speaking to me, none of them praying over me, and none greeting me."

He said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent down our repentance upon His Prophet ﷺ when the last third of the night remained, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was with Umm Salamah, and Umm Salamah was kind regarding my affair and attentive to my matter. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'O Umm Salamah, Kaʿb ibn Malik has been forgiven.' She said: 'Shall I not send to him to give him the good news?' He said: 'If you do, the people will crowd upon you and keep you from sleep for the rest of the night.'

Until, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the Fajr prayer, he announced the acceptance of Allah's repentance upon us." Related by al-Bukhari and Muslim.

Ibn Kathir said: "This is a sound, established hadith, agreed upon for its authenticity, and it comprises the explanation of the verse in the best and most extensive manner."

The second point: Some exegetes said: In the verse there is evidence of severity toward one who commits a sin, and of cutting off whatever distracts from obedience.

The third point: In the verse there is evidence of encouragement toward truthfulness.

Al-Qashani said: In His saying, ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah﴾, that is, from all vices by avoiding them, especially the vice of lying. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And be with the truthful﴾. Lying is the worst and most ugly of vices, for it contradicts manliness, and it has been said: "There is no manliness for one who lies," since the purpose of speech by which a human being is distinguished from the rest of the animals is to inform others of what they do not know. So when the report does not correspond to reality, the benefit of speech is not achieved, and a false belief arises from it, and that is among the properties of Satanic nature; thus the liar is a devil. Just as lying is the most ugly of vices, truthfulness is the most excellent of virtues, the root of every good, the material of every praiseworthy quality, the foundation of all goodness and happiness, and through it every perfection is attained. Its root is truthfulness in the covenant of Allah the Exalted, which is the outcome of fulfilling the covenant of innate nature or of the self, as He said: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with Allah﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 23], in the binding of resolve and the promise of creation. As He said of Isma'il: ﴿Indeed, he was true to his promise﴾ [Maryam: 54]. When it is observed in all circumstances, even in thought, intention, speech and action, dreams and inspirations, states and stations, gifts and witnessings become true, as if it were the root of the tree of perfection and the seed of the fruit of spiritual states. End.

Since He, the Exalted, made being with the truthful obligatory, He indicated that going forth with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is a collective obligation (fard kifayah), so it is not permissible for all to remain behind, and it is not required that all people go forth. Then He, glorified is He, said:

**The discussion of His words, exalted is He:**

[120] ﴿It was not fitting for the people of Madinah and the Bedouins around them to stay behind from the Messenger of God, or to prefer their own selves over his self. That is because no thirst, fatigue, or hunger afflicts them in the way of God, nor do they tread any ground that enrages the disbelievers, nor do they inflict any harm on an enemy, but a righteous deed is recorded for them by it. Indeed, God does not waste the reward of the good-doers.﴾

﴿It was not fitting for the people of Madinah﴾, meaning: it was not feasible for them to remain constantly with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his Companions. ﴿And the Bedouins around them﴾ [were not to] ﴿stay behind from the Messenger of God﴾, meaning: when he set out for the raid. ﴿Or prefer their own selves over his self﴾, meaning: they should not be stingy with their selves regarding what befalls his self; that is, they should not choose to preserve themselves over his self in hardships.

Al-Zamakhshari said: They were commanded to accompany him in adversity and hardship, to endure the terrors with him with desire, energy, and gladness, and to expose themselves to the hardships that his self undergoes, knowing that it is the most precious of selves to God and the most honoured by Him. So when it was exposed, along with its nobility and honour, to plunging into hardship and terror, it became obligatory upon all other selves to throw themselves into what it was exposed to, and for their owners not to care for them or give them any weight, and for them to be the lightest and least valued thing to them. This is apart from their [the owners'] holding themselves aloof from following it and accompanying it, and being stingy with them in what he himself has permitted to be given freely. 

This is an emphatic prohibition, along with a condemnation of their matter, a reproach to them for it, and an incitement to follow him with pride and zeal. End of quotation.

It has been narrated that Abu Dharr (may God be pleased with him) had his camel slow down with him, so he carried his belongings on his back and followed the trail of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on foot. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) saw his figure, he said: "Be Abu Dharr!" The people said: "It is he!" He said: "May God have mercy on Abu Dharr: he walks alone, dies alone, and will be raised alone."

It has also been narrated that Abu Khaythama al-Ansari (may God be pleased with him) reached his orchard, and he had a beautiful wife. She spread out [a mat] for him in the shade, spread the mat for him, and brought him dates and cold water.

He looked and said: "A shady shade, ripe dates, cold water, and a beautiful woman, while the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is in the heat and the wind! This is not good!" He stood up, saddled his she-camel, took his sword and spear, and went off like the wind. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) cast his gaze toward the road, and suddenly there was a rider whom the mirage was making appear [distant]. He said: "Be Abu Khaythama!" And so he was. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) rejoiced at him and asked God's forgiveness for him.

Al-Suhayli said in (*al-Rawd*): "*Kun Abu Dharr, kun Abu Khaythama*" has the wording of an imperative, but its meaning is like your saying "Aslim" (be safe), i.e., may God make you safe. End of quotation.

Likewise said others among the earlier scholars, such as al-Farisi. Al-Mutarrizi mentioned it in the saying of al-Hariri: "*Kun Abu Zayd*."

And in the poetry of Ibn Hilal:

> *And one who excuses (himself), whom God said of his beauty: "Be a trial for the worlds," and so he was.*

They did not elaborate on its explanation beyond this. It is a wondrous and strange construction, and its meaning is: God brought it to us and made it so that he would be the one who comes upon us. The cause is placed in the position of the effect in the form of a supplicatory, performative sentence, according to his saying in the hadith: "*Abli wa akhliq*" (wear it out and make it worn). That is: may God give you long life, and may God let you enjoy your garment until it wears out and becomes old.

And their saying "*Aslim*" means: may God make you safe so that you may be safe. Then, when it was put in its place, it was kept attributed to its doer, even though the one from whom the request is made is God. This is close to their saying "*A-raynaka hahuna*" (I will see you here), meaning: do not sit until I see you. It is either a figure of speech or a metonymy. Thus [it is stated] in (*al-Inaya*).

﴿That﴾ refers to what is indicated by his saying "*ma kana*" (it was not fitting) of the prohibition against staying behind, or the obligation of [sharing] the same [hardships]. ﴿Because they﴾, meaning: because of the reason that: ﴿no thirst afflicts them﴾, meaning: no part of thirst; ﴿nor fatigue﴾, meaning: exhaustion from the march, especially along with thirst; ﴿nor hunger﴾, meaning: starvation that weakens them from marching; ﴿in the way of God. Nor do they tread any ground﴾, meaning: they do not trample any place ﴿that enrages the disbelievers﴾, meaning: those who are the enemies of God. Angering the enemy brings about the satisfaction of his enemy. ﴿Nor do they inflict any harm on an enemy﴾, meaning: killing, defeat, or capture; ﴿but a righteous deed is recorded for them by it. Indeed, God does not waste the reward of the good-doers﴾, meaning: on account of their good-doing. This is a reason for "*kutiba*" (is recorded), and an indication that bearing hardships is a form of good-doing, because the purpose of it is to elevate the word of God, exalted is He.

(p-3298) On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[121] ﴿And they do not spend any expenditure, small or large, nor do they cross any valley, but it is recorded for them, so that Allah may reward them with the best of what they used to do.﴾

﴿And they do not spend any expenditure, small⁠﴾ means: such an amount does not cause hardship. ﴿Or large⁠﴾, like what ʿUthman (may Allah be pleased with him) spent at the expedition of Tabuk, which was one thousand dinars and three hundred camels with their saddle-cloths (aḥlās) and pack-saddles (aqtāb). ﴿Nor do they cross any valley⁠﴾ in their journey. The word wādī is every open depression through which the torrent passes. It is an active participle (ism fāʿil) from (wadiya), meaning "it flowed," so it was originally the torrent itself. Then the usage spread to its place, and then it became a true term for any land. Its plural is (awdiya), like nādin (a gathering place, with the plural ANDIYA) and nājin, whose plural is (anjiya). There is no fourth pattern for it in the speech of the Arabs.

﴿But it is recorded for them⁠﴾ means: a righteous deed is recorded for them through it. ﴿So that Allah may reward them with the best of what they used to do⁠﴾ means: so that He may reward them for every deed of theirs, whether complete or incomplete, with the reward of their best deeds. That is, if they incline with their souls away from the path, they miss that, and the accountability for them becomes more severe.

When Allah, exalted is He, had earlier explained the gravity of staying behind from the Messenger in jihad, and had intensified the warning against those who stayed behind and refused to march forth, He removed what might be imagined about the obligation of marching forth upon everyone, which would entail hardship and disruption of livelihood affairs, by stating that its obligation is collective (kifāʾī). So He, glorified is He, said:

**The commentary on His saying, Exalted is He:**

[ 122 ] ﴿It is not for the believers to go out all together. Why should not a party from every division of them go forth, so that they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them, so that they may beware?﴾

﴿It is not for the believers to go out all together﴾, meaning: it is not proper or right that they do so, such that their lands are left empty of people. ﴿Why should not a party go forth﴾, meaning: since it is not possible for everyone to go out, and it would not be in the public interest, then why should not ﴿a party from every division of them﴾ go forth, meaning: from every large group, a small group among them, who will suffice them for the going out (p-3299) ﴿to gain understanding in the religion﴾, meaning: to learn the matters of the religion from the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿And to warn their people﴾, meaning: to inform them and tell them what they have been commanded and forbidden. ﴿When they return to them﴾, meaning: from their military expedition. ﴿So that they may beware﴾, meaning: so that they may correct their deeds.

**Remarks:**

**First:** Al-Suyuti said in *al-Iklil*: The verse indicates that jihad is a communal obligation (*fard kifaya*), and that seeking understanding of the religion (*tafaqquh*), spreading knowledge, and teaching the ignorant are likewise. It also indicates travelling in pursuit of knowledge.

Some people used it as evidence for accepting the report of a single narrator (*khabar al-wahid*), because a *ta'ifa* (party) is a small group. Indeed, Mujahid said that it may be applied to a single person. End of quote.

Al-Jassas said in *al-Ahkam*: The verse indicates the binding force of the report of a single narrator in matters of religious practice that do not bind the general public and whose need is not widespread. This is because the party was commanded to warn, so the implication of the proof is included in two ways:

One: warning requires doing what one is commanded to do, otherwise it would not be a warning.

Second: God's command to us to beware upon the warning of the party, since the meaning of His saying ﴿so that they may beware﴾ is "so that they may be wary." This implies the obligation to act upon the report of a single narrator, because a *ta'ifa* applies to one person. So its proof is clear. End of quote.

In *al-Qamus*: a *ta'ifa* of a thing is a piece of it, or one or more, or up to a thousand, or at least two men, or one man; so it may mean "a single soul."

Al-Raghib said: When *ta'ifa* is intended as a plural, it is the plural of *ta'if*. When it is intended as singular, it may be a plural used to refer to one person, or it may be formed like *rawiya* and *alama* and similar words.

**Second:** If it is asked: the apparent wording would have been, "so that they may gain understanding in the religion, and teach their people when they return to them, so that they may understand." Why was "warning" put in place of "teaching," and "they may beware" in place of "they may understand"?

It is answered: this indicates the purpose of it, which is acquiring fear of God and wariness of His punishment.

Al-Ghazali, may God have mercy on him, said: In the first age, the term *fiqh* was the name for the knowledge of the Hereafter, knowing the subtle diseases of the souls and the corruption of deeds, comprehending the worthlessness of this world, the intense longing for the bliss of the Hereafter, and the dominance of fear over the heart. This verse indicates it. Thus in *al-Inaya*. 

Al-Zamakhshari said regarding the verse: They should make their aim and the target of their resolve in *tafaqquh* the warning of their people, guiding them, and advising them, not the base aims that jurists pursue, and the worthless goals they aim at: seeking leading positions and dominance, spreading themselves throughout the lands, imitating the oppressors in their clothing and mounts, competing with one another, the spread of jealousy among them, the eyes of one of them bulging when he glances at another's school or a group, falling on their knees before him, and his eagerness to have his heels trodden upon by all people. How far these are from the saying of the Mighty and Majestic:

﴿The abode of the Hereafter We assign to those who do not desire exaltation in the earth or corruption﴾ [al-Qasas: 83]. End of quote.

**Third:** Al-Qashani said regarding the verse: It is obligatory upon every capable person in a group to follow the path of seeking knowledge, since it is not possible for all of them to do so: outwardly, because of the loss of benefits, and inwardly, because of lack of readiness.

Then he said: *Tafaqquh* in the religion is of the knowledge of the heart, not of acquired knowledge, since not everyone who acquires knowledge comprehends, as He said: ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings lest they understand it﴾ [al-Isra: 46]. The coverings are the natural veils and the psychological barriers. Whoever wishes to comprehend should go forth in the way of God and follow the path of purification and clarification, until knowledge appears from his heart onto his tongue. Thus the intended *tafaqquh* is knowledge firmly rooted in the heart, its roots struck deep into the soul, its effect clearly visible on the limbs, such that its possessor cannot commit what contradicts that knowledge; otherwise he would not be a knower.

Do you not see how God denied understanding to those whose fear of God did not overcome their fear of people, by His saying: ﴿Indeed, you are more fearsome in their breasts than God. That is because they are a people who do not understand﴾ [al-Hashr: 13], because the fear of God is necessarily tied to knowledge, as He said: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear God﴾ [Fatir: 28]. And He denied knowledge to those who do not act upon it, in His saying: ﴿Are those who know equal to those who do not know?﴾ [al-Zumar: 9]. When they comprehend, and their knowledge appears upon their limbs, it affects others, and they are affected by it, because they have been nourished by it and it oozes from them, as was the case with the Messenger of God (ﷺ). So the warning, which is its purpose, becomes necessary. End of quote.

When, at the beginning of the surah, God commanded the disavowal of the polytheists of the Arabs and fighting them, and then explained the conditions and disgraceful acts of the hypocrites, He pointed to its conclusion with what matches its opening with that, so He, glorified be He, said:

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[123] ﴿O you who have believed, fight those adjacent to you of the disbelievers, and let them find in you harshness. And know that Allah is with the righteous.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, fight those adjacent to you of the disbelievers﴾ That is, those who are near to you, and they are the polytheists of the Arabian Peninsula, as we have said.

As for His words, exalted is He, ﴿and let them find in you harshness﴾, they said: it is a comprehensive term encompassing boldness, patience in fighting, intensity of enmity, and severity in killing and taking captives.

Its apparent meaning is a command to the disbelievers that they should find harshness in the believers, but the intended meaning is a command to the believers to adopt qualities such as patience and what accompanies it, so that the disbelievers find them characterized by these qualities. It is according to the saying of the people: "I shall not see you here."

Al-ghilzah (harshness) is the opposite of tenderness (al-riqqah). It is read with a ghayn that may be vowelled in three ways (ghilzah, ghalzah, ghilzah), and it has been recited thus, but the Seven Readers [recite it] with the kasrah (ghilzah).

﴿And know that Allah is with the righteous﴾ That is, with support and aid.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[124] ﴿And whenever a surah is revealed, among them are those who say, "Which of you has had its faith increased by this?" As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice.﴾

﴿And whenever a surah is revealed﴾ means: a portion of the Qur'an, inimitable and encompassing a body of proofs and the removal of doubts. ﴿Among them﴾ means: among the hypocrites. ﴿Are those who say﴾ means: some of them say to others, ﴿"Which of you has had its faith increased by this"﴾, that is, by this surah, in denial and mockery of the believers, and in their belief that faith increases through increase in knowledge gained from revelation and acting upon it. ﴿As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith﴾ because it adds to certainty and firmness, and is more soothing to the heart, owing to the abundance of proofs and the removal of doubts. ﴿And they rejoice﴾ means: at its descent and at the religious and worldly benefits it contains.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[125] ﴿And as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it adds filth to their filth, and they die while they are disbelievers.﴾

﴿And as for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ i.e., disbelief and corrupt belief. ﴿it adds filth to their filth﴾ i.e., their disbelief in it (the surah) added to their disbelief in other than it. ﴿and they die while they are disbelievers﴾ i.e., that disbelief became firmly established in them, by means of this increase, until their death.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[126] ﴿Do they not see that they are tested every year, once or twice? Yet they do not repent, nor do they take heed.﴾

﴿Do they not see﴾ — meaning the hypocrites — ﴿that they are tested﴾, i.e., they are afflicted by the exposure of their deceit and treachery, (p-3303) or by the breaking of their covenant, ﴿every year, once or twice. Yet they do not repent﴾, i.e., from their conduct and their breaking of their covenant, ﴿nor do they take heed﴾, i.e., they do not admonish themselves by the fact that these are decisive signs, and that the testing comes about because of their opposition to them.

Then He explained their condition when it was revealed while they were in the assembly where the revelation was being conveyed, following the statement of their speech, while they were absent from it, by His saying, may He be exalted:

The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 9, verse 127:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[127] ﴿And whenever a surah is revealed, some of them look at others, [saying], "Does anyone see you?" Then they turn away. Allah has turned their hearts away because they are a people who do not understand.﴾

﴿And whenever a surah is revealed, some of them look at others, [saying], "Does anyone see you?"﴾

al-Zamakhshari said: That is, they winked at one another with their eyes, denying the revelation and mocking it, saying: "Does anyone of the Muslims see you, so that we may leave? For we cannot endure listening to it, and laughter overcomes us, and we fear exposure among them." Or they exchanged glances, conferring about how to arrange their departure and slipping away furtively (lawadhan). They say: "Does anyone see you?" ﴿Then they turn away﴾, that is, away from the assembly of revelation, out of fear of exposure. ﴿Allah has turned their hearts﴾, that is, away from faith, in proportion to their turning away from his presence, peace be upon him.

The sentence is either informative or supplicatory. ﴿Because they﴾, that is, because ﴿they are a people who do not understand﴾, that is, they do not contemplate the command of Allah so as to comprehend it.

Remarks:

The first: The preceding verse indicates an increase in faith through what has been mentioned, and whether we say that deeds are included in the designation of faith, which is the truth, or not, and that it is merely inner assent, increase is undoubtedly accepted. The first is self-evident, and the second is likewise, since the faith of the Prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, and of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, is not like the faith of others, and this is not doubted.

The second: Allah mentioned two of the disgraces of the hypocrites: their failure to take heed from trials, and the entrenchment of disbelief in them (p-3304) and its increase at a time that calls for an increase in faith, which is the repetition of revelation.

Since the purpose was to clarify their persistence in their disbelief and the failure of admonitions to benefit them, He concluded their disgraces with this, because it is its result, and He placed before it what befalls them of trials, because in it is a great deterrent, if they had remembered.

Al-Qashani has been subtle in clarifying this, with the existence of affirmation in it, and his expression is:

Trial is a guide from Allah, exalted is He, who leads people to Him. It has been related in a hadith: "Trial is a whip of the whips of Allah, exalted is He, by which He drives His servants toward Him." For every illness, poverty, and ill condition that befalls a person breaks the force of his self and its powers, and suppresses its qualities and desires, so the heart softens, emerges from its veil, becomes uneasy with inclining to this world and its pleasures, withdraws from them and recoils, and so turns toward Allah.

The least of its degrees is that when he perceives that there is no escape from it except to Him, and finds no refuge or shelter from trial other than Him, he humbles himself before Him and abases himself in His presence, as He said: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shadows, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Luqman: 32] ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side or sitting or standing﴾ [Yunus: 12].

In sum, it necessitates the softening of the veil or its removal, so let him seize the moment and seek refuge, and let him form a habit to which he always returns until alertness and remembrance become firm, and repentance and presence become easy, so that he does not grow accustomed to heedlessness upon deliverance and be overcome by it, and the self is not strengthened in security and the veil does not become thicker than it was, as He said: ﴿But when He delivers them to the land, they immediately associate others [with Him]﴾ [al-Ankabut: 65] ﴿So when We removed his harm from him, he passed on as though he had never called Us concerning a harm that touched him﴾ [Yunus: 12]. End.

The third: al-Suyuti said in (al-Iklil): Ibn Abbas drew from His saying ﴿then they turned away﴾ the disapproval of saying "I turned away from the prayer" - related by Ibn Abi Hatim.

The source of this returns to a verbal courtesy, avoiding what may give a wrong impression, or what is used to censure the disobedient.

(p-3305) The Imam Ibn al-Qayyim has devoted in (Zad al-Ma'ad) a section on the guidance of the Prophet ﷺ in guarding speech and choosing words, so let it be consulted.

Then Allah, exalted is He, explained what He bestowed upon the believers of the sending of the Seal of the Prophets, with His saying:

The commentary on His words, exalted is He:

[128] ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; it grieves him that you suffer hardship; he is anxious over you; toward the believers, he is kind and merciful.﴾

﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾, i.e., a great Messenger of your own kind and of your own lineage, an Arab, a Qurashi like you, just as Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: ﴿Our Lord, raise among them a Messenger from among themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 129], and God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Certainly did Allah confer favor upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 164].

Ja'far ibn Abi Talib spoke to the Najashi (the Negus), and al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba spoke to the envoy of Kisra, and they said:

"Indeed Allah has sent among us a Messenger from ourselves, whose lineage we know, and his description, his entry and his exit, and his truthfulness and his trustworthiness." The hadith (continues).

Then He, exalted is He, mentioned, by His words, what follows from kinship and affinity in terms of consequences: ﴿it grieves him that you suffer hardship﴾, i.e., it is severe and burdensome for him, because he is a part of you, your distress and your encountering of what is disliked; so he fears for you the evil consequence and falling into punishment. ﴿He is anxious over you﴾, i.e., over your guidance, so that none of you turns away from following him and from seeking happiness through the religion of truth that he brought. ﴿Toward the believers, he is kind﴾, as he calls them to what saves them from punishment by warning against sins and disobediences, out of the excess of his compassion. ﴿Merciful﴾, as he overflows upon them with knowledge, recognitions, and perfections that bring them near, through teaching and encouraging them toward these, by his mercy.

(p-٣٣٠٦) The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[129] ﴿But if they turn away, say, "Allah is sufficient for me. There is no deity except Him. In Him I have placed my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne."﴾

﴿But if they turn away﴾, i.e., they turn away from faith in you and oppose you. ﴿Then say, "Allah is sufficient for me"﴾, i.e., seek help from Him and entrust your affairs to Him, for He is sufficient for you and your helper against them.

Al-Qashani said: That is, I have no need of you or of your help, just as a person has no need for a diseased, rotting limb that must rationally be amputated. That is, Allah is sufficient for me, so there is no one who has influence other than Him, and no helper except Him, as He says: ﴿There is no deity except Him. In Him I have placed my trust﴾, i.e., I have entrusted my affair to Him and I am confident in Him. ﴿And He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne﴾, i.e., nothing is outside His encompassing, and His judgment and command come from Him to all things. The Throne is singled out because it is the greatest of the created beings, so whatever is below it is included. It was also recited as (al-ʿaẓīmu, العَظِيمُ) in the nominative case, making it an attribute of the Lord, glorious and exalted is He.

Completed what we wrote on the morning of Monday, 24 Rajab 1322 AH, at the threshold of the Sananiyya Mosque in Damascus, al-Sham. O Allah, by Your grace, make the completion easy for us. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon the Master of the Messengers, Muhammad, and all his family, until the Day of Judgement.
